title: Ezekiel's Vision Was Lowkey Insane
paragraphs: So, when I was 30, I was living with the other exiles by the Kebar River. On the fifth day of the fourth month, the sky literally just opened up and I started seeing these wild visions of God.

(Just to be clear, it was the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year since King Jehoiachin got exiled. That's when God's word came straight to me, Ezekiel, son of Buzi the priest, right there on the banks of the Kebar River in Babylon. God's power just hit me that day.)

I looked up and saw this insane dust storm coming from the north—a massive cloud with lightning flashing everywhere, and a huge ball of fire that was glowing like shiny bronze. Inside the fire, there were these four living creatures that looked so alive. They basically had a human shape, but each one had four faces and four wings. Their legs were super sturdy and straight, like pillars, but their feet were like calf hooves that sparkled like polished bronze in the fire. They had human hands under their wings on all four sides. All four of them had these faces and wings, and their wings touched the creature next to them. They didn't turn or anything; they just moved straight forward.

Their faces were pretty wild: the front one was a human face, the one on the right was a lion's face, the one on the left was an ox's face, and the one in the back was an eagle's face. So yeah, that's the deal with the faces. Their wings were spread out, with one pair touching the wings of the creatures on either side, and the other pair covering their own bodies. Each one just went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit guided them, that's where they went, without even turning.

The four creatures themselves looked like a blazing fire, or maybe like torches. Flames were shooting back and forth between them, and lightning bolts were zapping out of the fire. The creatures were zipping around as fast as lightning strikes.

As I was watching these four creatures, I saw what looked like a wheel on the ground next to each of them. The wheels were all identical, sparkling like diamonds. It was like they were wheels inside of wheels, kind of like a gyroscope.

They could move in any of the four directions they were facing, but always straight, never swerving. The rims of the wheels were huge and were covered in eyes all the way around. When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them. When the creatures lifted off the ground, the wheels lifted off too. Wherever the spirit went, they went, and the wheels were right there with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels. When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stopped, the wheels stopped; and when they lifted off the ground, the wheels lifted off with them, because the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

Above the heads of the living creatures was this dome-like thing, shimmering like a sky made of crystal, stretched out over them. Under the dome, they each had one set of wings stretched out toward the others, and another set covering their bodies. When they moved, I heard their wings, and it sounded like a massive waterfall, like the voice of God Almighty, or like the noise of a whole army on a battlefield. When they stopped, they just folded their wings.

And then, while they were standing there with their wings folded, a voice came from above the dome over their heads. Above the dome was something that looked like a throne, the color of a sapphire, and on the throne was a figure that looked human, but was towering over it. From the waist up, he looked like glowing bronze, and from the waist down, he looked like a blazing fire. There was this incredible brightness all around him! It looked just like a rainbow on a rainy day. And then it hit me—it was the Glory of God!
When I saw all that, I just dropped to my knees and put my face on the ground. Then I heard a voice speaking.

title: God's Super Intense Job Offer
paragraphs: Then a voice said, “Son of man, get up. I need to talk to you.”
The second that voice spoke, the Spirit just zapped into me and got me on my feet. I was actually listening as He talked to me.

He said, “Son of man, I’m sending you to the Israelites, who are lowkey the most rebellious crew ever. For real, they and their ancestors have been staging a rebellion right up to this very day. These people I’m sending you to are a tough crowd—super stubborn in their ways. You gotta tell them, ‘This is a message from the Lord GOD.’ They're a defiant bunch. So, whether they listen to you or not, at least they’ll know a real prophet was among them. But for real, don't be scared of them, son of man, and don't let their words get to you. Don't be afraid even if living with them feels like stepping on thorns or finding scorpions in your bed. Don't freak out over their mean words or their angry stares. They're just a bunch of rebels. Your job is to speak my words to them. It's not on you if they listen or not. They're just that stubborn.
“Just make sure, son of man, that you don’t start acting rebellious like them. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”

And when I looked, His hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll. He unrolled it, and on both sides, front and back, were written songs of sadness, mourning, and total doom. It was a major downer.

title: I Ate a Book & Became God's Watchman
paragraphs: He told me, “Yo, son of man, eat what you see. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the family of Israel.”
As I opened my mouth, he gave me the scroll to eat, saying, “Son of man, eat this book that I am giving you. Make a full meal of it!”
So I ate it. It tasted so good—just like honey.

Then he told me, “Son of man, go to the family of Israel and speak my Message. Look, I’m not sending you to a people who speak a hard-to-learn language with words you can hardly pronounce. If I had sent you to such people, their ears would have perked up and they would have listened immediately.

“But it won’t work that way with the family of Israel. They won’t listen to you because they won’t listen to me. They are, as I said, a hard case, hardened in their sin. But I’ll make you as hard in your way as they are in theirs. I’ll make your face as hard as rock, harder than granite. Don’t let them intimidate you. Don’t be afraid of them, even though they’re a bunch of rebels.”

Then he said, “Son of man, get all these words that I’m giving you inside you. Listen to them obediently. Make them your own. And now go. Go to the exiles, your people, and speak. Tell them, ‘This is the Message of God, the Master.’ Speak your piece, whether they listen or not.”

Then the Spirit picked me up. Behind me I heard a great commotion—“Blessed be the Glory of God in his Sanctuary!”—the wings of the living creatures beating against each other, the whirling wheels, the rumble of a great earthquake.

The Spirit lifted me and took me away. I went bitterly and angrily. I didn’t want to go. But God had me in his grip. I arrived among the exiles who lived near the Kebar River at Tel Abib. I came to where they were living and sat there for seven days, appalled.
At the end of the seven days, I received this Message from God:

“Son of man, I’ve made you a watchman for the family of Israel. Whenever you hear me say something, warn them for me. If I say to the wicked, ‘You are going to die,’ and you don’t sound the alarm warning them that it’s a matter of life or death, they will die and it will be your fault. I’ll hold you responsible. But if you warn the wicked and they keep right on sinning anyway, they’ll most certainly die for their sin, but you won’t die. You’ll have saved your life.

“And if the righteous turn back from living righteously and take up with evil when I step in and put them in a hard place, they’ll die. If you haven’t warned them, they’ll die because of their sins, and none of the right things they’ve done will count for anything—and I’ll hold you responsible. But if you warn these righteous people not to sin and they listen to you, they’ll live because they took the warning—and again, you’ll have saved your life.”
God grabbed me by the shoulder and said, “Get up. Go out on the plain. I want to talk with you.”
So I got up and went out on the plain. I couldn’t believe my eyes: the Glory of God! Right there! It was like the Glory I had seen at the Kebar River. I fell to the ground, prostrate.

Then the Spirit entered me and put me on my feet. He said, “Go home and shut the door behind you.” And then something odd: “Son of man: They’ll tie you hand and foot with ropes so you can’t leave the house. I’ll make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so you won’t be able to talk and tell the people what they’re doing wrong, even though they are a bunch of rebels.

“But then when the time is ripe, I’ll free your tongue and you’ll say, ‘This is what God, the Master, says: . . .’ From then on it’s up to them. They can listen or not listen, whichever they like. They are a bunch of rebels!”

title: Ezekiel's 430-Day Performance Art Was WILD
paragraphs: “Alright, son of man, grab a brick and put it in front of you. On this brick, I want you to draw a map of Jerusalem. Then, you’re gonna stage a whole siege against this brick-city. Build mini siege walls, a ramp, set up little army camps, and place tiny battering rams all around it. Next, grab an iron skillet and stand it up on its side between you and the city, like an iron wall. You need to face this model city. It’s under siege, and you’re the one leading the attack. This whole setup is a huge sign for the people of Israel.

“Next, you’re gonna lie down on your left side, and you’re going to place all the sin of the nation of Israel right on yourself. You have to bear their sin for the exact number of days you’re lying on that side. The number of days will match the years of their sin—that’s 390 years. So for 390 days, you will carry the sin of the nation of Israel.

“Then, once you’re done with that, you’re gonna flip over and lie on your right side to bear the sin of the nation of Judah. This time, your assignment is to lie there for forty days, one day for each year of their sin. You have to look straight at your siege of Jerusalem model. Roll up your sleeve, shake your fist at it, and preach against the city.
“I’m gonna tie you up with ropes, so tight that you can’t move or even turn over until you’ve completed all the days of this siege performance.

“Okay, now for your food. I want you to get some wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Mix them all together in a bowl to make a kind of flatbread. This is your food ration for the 390 days you’re lying on your side. You’ll measure out about half a pound for each day and eat it right on schedule. You’ll also get a daily ration of about a pint of water, and you have to drink that on schedule too. You’ll eat this bread like a barley loaf, but here’s the crazy part: you have to bake it out in public where everyone can see you, using dried human dung for fuel.”

God then said, “This is a picture of what the people of Israel are going to do. Among the foreign nations where I will send them, they will have to eat foods that are totally forbidden for a holy people.”

I immediately said, “No way, God, my Master! Never! I’ve never made myself unclean with food like that. Ever since I was a kid, I’ve never eaten anything the law forbids, nothing I found dead or that was attacked by wild animals. I have never taken a single bite of forbidden food.”
“Alright,” he said. “I’ll let you bake your bread over cow dung instead of human dung.”

Then he said to me, “Son of man, I’m about to cut off the entire food supply from Jerusalem. The people will be on starvation rations, constantly worrying where their next meal is coming from, and desperately searching for their next sip of water. It’s going to be a full-blown famine. People will just stare at each other, seeing nothing but skin and bones, and they’ll just be in despair. This is what sin leads to.”

title: God's Judgment Goes Viral
paragraphs: “Alright, God says to take a sharp sword and use it like a razor to shave your head and your beard. Then, get some scales and divide the hair into three equal parts. When the siege is finally over, you’re gonna take one-third of the hair and burn it right in the middle of the city. Take the second third, chop it up with that sword, and sprinkle it all around the city. The last third, you’re just gonna throw it to the wind. And then I’m gonna come after them with a sword.

“But hold up, grab a few of those hairs and stick them in your pocket. Then take some of *those* hairs and toss them into the fire—burn ‘em up. From that fire, a new fire will spread to the whole family of Israel.

“This is what the Lord God is saying: This is Jerusalem we’re talking about. I put her at the center of the world, with all the nations surrounding her. But she rebelled against my laws and rules, and honestly, she was way worse than all the nations around her—just straight-up wicked. She refused my guidance and ignored my directions.

“So, the Lord God says: You’ve been more stubborn and rebellious than any of the nations around you, ignoring my rules and directions. You’ve actually sunk down to the low level of the people around you.

“So, the Lord God says this: I’m turning against you, Jerusalem. Yeah, you. I’m going to punish you right in front of all the other nations. Because of all your disgusting idols, I’m going to do something to you that I’ve never done before and will never do again: families are going to become cannibals. Parents will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. That’s some serious punishment. And anyone who’s left, I’ll just scatter them to the winds.

“Therefore, as sure as I am the living God—this is a decree from the Lord God—because you’ve defiled my Holy Temple with your disgusting and obscene idols, I’m out. I won’t show you even an ounce of pity. A third of your people will die from disease or starvation inside the city, a third will be killed by the sword outside the city, and the last third will be scattered to the winds, chased by killers.
“Only after all that will my anger finally cool down. Then you’ll know that I, the Lord, was serious about all this, that I’m a jealous God who you don’t mess with.

“When I’m done with you, you’ll be nothing but a pile of ruins. The nations passing by will make jokes about you. When I’m finished with my angry punishment and harsh rebukes, you’ll be a total joke, a horror story that all the surrounding nations tell. I, the Lord, have said it.

“And when I start shooting my deadly arrows of famine at you, I’ll be shooting to kill. Then I’ll crank up the famine and cut off your food supply completely. Famine after famine—and then I’ll send wild animals to finish off your children. Sickness, murder, death—and I’ll be the one who sent it. I, the Lord, have spoken.”

title: God's Final Warning: Idol Worship Canceled
paragraphs: Then God's word hit me. He was like, 'Yo, son of man, turn toward the mountains of Israel and call them out. Tell 'em: 'Hey, mountains of Israel, listen up to what the Lord GOD has to say.' The Master, GOD, is talking to all you mountains, hills, canyons, and valleys: I'm about to wreck your pagan shrines. I'm gonna tear down your altars, smash your sun-god statues, and your people are gonna drop dead right while they're bowing to your fake idols. I'll pile up the bodies of the Israelites right in front of those useless idols and scatter their bones all around your shrines. Every single town you live in will be left in ruins and the pagan spots will be totally demolished—altars wrecked, idols shattered, and all those custom sun-god pillars you love so much will be toast. Dead bodies everywhere. Then you'll finally get that I am the real GOD.

But I'll let a few of you survive the slaughter as you get scattered across other countries. In those foreign lands where they're taken as prisoners, they'll remember me. They'll finally realize how crushed I was by their cheating hearts, by their crazy lust for other gods. They'll be totally disgusted with themselves for all the evil, messed-up stuff they did. They'll know for sure that I am GOD. They'll get that my warning of judgment wasn't just some empty threat.

This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stomp your feet, and scream, 'No, no, no!' because of all the disgusting, evil things happening in Israel. They're about to die by violence, by starvation, by sickness—death is coming for everyone. People far away will die, people nearby will be killed, and whoever is left in the city will starve. Why? Because I am so, so angry. They'll know I'm GOD when they see their own people's dead bodies scattered all around their busted sex-and-religion shrines, on every hill and under every green tree where they got into their weird rituals. I'm gonna bring my power down hard on them, completely destroy the country wherever they live, and turn it into a wasteland from the desert all the way to Riblah. Then they'll know that I am GOD!'

title: It's Officially Over for Israel
paragraphs: God's Word hit me. He said, "Yo, son of man—God, the Boss, has a message for Israel:

"It's the end. Like, the end of normal life for everyone. It's all over. The end is coming for you. I'm unleashing my anger on you. I've made my decision based on how you've been living, and I'm gonna make you pay for all the nasty stuff you've done. I'm not gonna look away or feel bad for you. You're gonna get what you deserve for your lifestyle. All that gross stuff you did? It's gonna come right back at you, and then you'll know for real that I am God."

"I, God, the Boss, am telling you: Disaster after disaster! Look, it's coming! It's the end—the end is here. The end is ripe. Watch out, it's on its way! This is your destiny, all you people living in this land. Time's up. It's go-time. No more excuses, no more asking for extra time. I'm about to pour out my fury on you, let out all my anger, judge you for how you've lived, and make you pay for all your disgusting actions. I'm not gonna look the other way or feel sorry for you. I'm making you pay for your lifestyle. Your disgusting actions are gonna boomerang back on you. And then you'll realize that it's me, God, who's bringing the hammer down.

"'Judgment Day! Your fate is sealed. The leadership is way too full of itself, pride is off the charts, and violence is strutting around like it owns the place, waving its evil stick. But it's all for nothing, and nothing will be left of them. Time's up. The final countdown... The person buying stuff shouldn't be bragging, and the person selling shouldn't be stressing. Why? Because my judgment and anger have flipped the whole world upside down. The whole market has crashed. It's never going back to the way it was. And don't even think about the market bouncing back. The whole country is broke because of its sins, and it's not getting any better.

"'The trumpet sounds for battle: 'Get ready!' But nobody is actually going to fight. My anger has them all frozen! If you're on the roads, you get killed. If you go home, you die of starvation or sickness. You either get murdered out in the country or die from being sick or hungry in the city. The ones who survive will run for the hills. They'll be crying like doves in the valleys, each one crying over their own sins.

"'Every hand is just hanging there, totally weak, and everyone's knees are like jelly. They're all wearing scratchy burlap clothes—looking like sad scarecrows. They're all shady and embarrassed, with their heads shaved bald in shame.

"'They're chucking their money in the streets. Their hard-earned cash smells like actual garbage. They realize it can't buy them anything they want or need on Judgment Day. They literally tripped over their money and fell into sin. They were so proud and extra with their jewelry, using it to decorate their fake, gross idols. So I'm gonna make those disgusting idols stink. I'm gonna give away all their religious stuff—strangers will just take it for free, and godless people will spit on it and make fun of it. I'm gonna turn my face away so I don't have to see my special place and people get trashed, as violent strangers just walk in and wreck everything. It's gonna be a bloodbath, with crime and violence filling the city. I'll bring in the worst kinds of people to take over their houses. I'll shut down all the bragging and showing off from the rich and powerful, and I'll make sure there's nothing holy left in their holy places. It's a total disaster. They'll be looking for peace, but there's no peace anywhere. Just one disaster after another, and rumors spreading like crazy. They'll be begging the prophet to tell them what's going on, but nobody will know anything. The priests will be clueless, and the elders won't know what to say. The king will be in despair, and the prince will be totally wrecked. The regular people will be paralyzed with fear, unable to move. I'm gonna deal with them right where they are and judge them by their own standards. Then they'll know that I am God.'"

title: God's Temple Got WEIRD...
paragraphs: So, picture this: It's the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day. I'm just chilling at my place, having a meeting with the leaders of Judah, when BAM! The hand of God just grabs me. I look up, and I'm shook. There's this figure that looks like a dude—fiery from the waist down and like super shiny bronze from the waist up. He reaches out a hand, grabs me by the hair (wild, right?), and the Spirit just swept me up into the air. Next thing I know, I'm in a vision, flying to Jerusalem. I land right at the north gate of the Temple's inner court, where they'd set up this statue of a pagan goddess that totally ticks God off. And right there in front of me is the Glory of God, just like I saw it on the plain. It was insane.
He tells me, “Son of man, look north.” So I do, and there it is. Just north of the entrance, this altar for that pagan goddess, Asherah, the one that makes God so mad.

Then he said, “Son of man, you seeing this? It's messed up. And they're doing it right here in my house! It's so bad it makes me want to just bounce from my own Temple. But trust me, you're about to see even crazier stuff.”
He took me to the entrance of the Temple court. I looked, and there was this big hole in the wall.
He said, “Son of man, dig through the wall.”
So I dug through the wall and found a door.
He said, “Alright, go through the door and see the messed-up things they're into.”

I went in and I couldn't believe what I was seeing. The walls were covered in paintings of reptiles, animals, and monsters—basically the whole squad of Egyptian gods—and the Israelites were worshiping them. In the middle of the room were seventy of Israel's leaders, with this guy Jaazaniah son of Shaphan front and center. They were all holding these incense things, and the smoke was just rising up in a cloud.

He said, “Son of man, you see what your leaders are doing in the dark? Each one is bowing down to his favorite god-picture. They're telling themselves, ‘God can't see us. God has bailed on our country.’”
Then he said, “You're about to see something even worse.”

He took me to the north gate entrance of God's Temple. And I saw women just sitting there, crying for Tammuz, some Babylonian fertility god. He was like, “You getting a good look, son of man? Because you're about to see something even more messed up.”

Finally, he took me to the inner court of God's Temple. And there, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five guys. They had their backs to God's Temple, and they were facing east, bowing down and worshiping the sun.

He said, “You've seen enough, son of man? Isn't it bad enough that Judah is doing all this wild stuff? They've filled the country with violence, and now they're provoking me even more with these disrespectful gestures. That's it. They've got an angry God on their hands now. No more mercy. They can cry and shout all they want, but I'm not even listening.”

title: Marked for Life or Death
paragraphs: Then I heard this booming voice shout, “Alright, executioners, get over here! And don’t forget your weapons.”

And just like that, six guys came down the road from the north gate, each one carrying a seriously deadly weapon. Another guy was with them, dressed in linen clothes and carrying a writer’s case. They all went inside and stood by the bronze altar.

The Glory of the God of Israel, which was usually chilling above the cherubim angels, moved to the entrance of the Temple. He called out to the guy in linen with the writer's case: “Go all through Jerusalem and put a mark on the forehead of everyone who is genuinely upset and grieving over all the terrible things happening in the city.”

Then I heard him tell the executioners, “Follow him through the city and start killing. Don’t feel sorry for anyone. Show zero mercy. Kill everyone—old men, women, young people, mothers, and children. But do not touch anyone who has the mark. Start right here at my Temple.”
So they started with the leaders who were right in front of the Temple.
He told the executioners, “Trash the Temple. Fill it up with dead bodies. Then go out and keep killing.” So they went out and started wrecking the city.

While this whole massacre was happening, I was the only one left. I just fell on my face and prayed, “Oh no, God, my Master! Are you really going to wipe out every single person left in Israel as you pour out your anger on Jerusalem?”

He replied, “The sin of Israel and Judah is off the charts. The whole country is full of murder, and the city is overflowing with injustice. They all keep saying, ‘God has bailed on us. He doesn’t see what we’re doing.’ Well, I do see, and I’m not feeling sorry for any of them. They’re about to get what they deserve for their actions.”
Just then, the man in linen with the writer’s case came back and said, “I did what you told me to do.”

title: God's Glory is Leaving the Temple?!
paragraphs: So I looked up again, and whoa! Right above the heads of those cherubim-angel creatures, there was this thing that looked just like a throne, all sparkly and blue like a sapphire. It was wild.
Then God told the guy in the linen outfit, "Yo, go into the middle of those wheels under the cherubim. Grab a handful of burning coals from there and just toss 'em all over the city."

I saw him go in. The cherubim were just chilling on the south side of the Temple when he walked in. Suddenly, this massive cloud filled up the inner courtyard. Then, God's Glory, like this super bright presence, lifted up from the cherubim and moved to the entrance of the Temple. The whole place, the court and the Temple, were just lit up with God's blazing glory. And the sound was insane! You could hear the cherubim's wings all the way from the outer court—it sounded like God's powerful voice, like thunder.

When God ordered the guy in linen, "Get some fire from between the wheels, from the cherubim," he went and stood next to a wheel. One of the cherubim reached into the fire, grabbed some coals, and put them in the guy's hands. He took them and left. And get this, you could see something that looked like a human hand under the cherubim's wings.

Then I saw four wheels next to the cherubim, one for each of them. The wheels were sparkling like crazy, like diamonds in the sun. All four looked the same, and it was like a wheel inside another wheel. When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions but always in a straight line. Wherever the cherubim went, the wheels followed. The cherubim were covered in eyes—on their backs, hands, and wings. The wheels were full of eyes too. I heard someone call the wheels "wheels within wheels."
Each cherub had four faces: the first was an angel's face, the second a human's, the third a lion's, and the fourth an eagle's.

Then the cherubim flew up. They were the same living creatures I had seen before by the Kebar River. When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. When they spread their wings to fly, the wheels stuck right by them. When they stopped, the wheels stopped. When they went up, the wheels went up, because the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

Then God's Glory left the Temple entrance and just hovered over the cherubim. I watched as the cherubim spread their wings and took off, with the wheels right there with them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the Temple, and the Glory of the God of Israel was right there above them.

These were the exact same creatures I had seen under the God of Israel by the Kebar River. I knew they were cherubim. Each one had four faces and four wings, and under their wings, they had what looked like human hands. Their faces were identical to the ones I saw by the Kebar River. They all just moved straight ahead.

title: You're NOT the Main Character
paragraphs: Then the Spirit just teleported me to the east gate of the Temple. Standing there were 25 dudes, and I totally recognized the leaders, Jaazaniah and Pelatiah.

God was like, "Son of man, these are the guys who are basically masterminds for sin, always cooking up some new evil scheme in the city. They’re out here saying, ‘We can do whatever we want. We're the important ones, the best part of the soup.’"
"Go up against them, son of man. Preach the truth to them."

Then God's Spirit came on me and gave me the words to say: "This is what God's telling you: ‘That’s a nice little speech for the public, Israel, but I know what you’re really thinking. You’ve murdered so many people in this city. The streets are literally piled with bodies because of you.’

"So, here's the deal from the Master, God: ‘Those bodies you piled up in the streets? *They're* the meat in this soup pot of a city, and you're not even in it. I'm kicking you out! You're scared of war? Well, guess what's coming for you. I'm bringing war right to your doorstep. I'm kicking you out of this city, handing you over to your enemies, and you're gonna get punished, big time. You'll die in battle. I'll bring my judgment on you at the very border of Israel. Then you'll finally get that I am God. This city isn't your safe little soup pot, and you're definitely not the prime cuts of meat in it. Not even close. I'll judge you at Israel's border, and you'll realize that I am God, because you blew off all my rules and commands. Instead of following me, you just copied the messed-up ways of the nations around you.’"

While I was still preaching, Pelatiah son of Benaiah just dropped dead. I hit the ground, face down, and yelled out, "Oh, Master, GOD! Are you really going to wipe out every last person left in Israel?"

Then God's message came back to me: "Son of man, your family—and I mean all the people of Israel who are in exile with you—are the ones the people in Jerusalem are dissing. They're saying, ‘Ha, they're far away from God. This land is ours now.’

"So, tell them this: ‘Here’s a message from the Master, God. Yeah, it's true I sent you far away and scattered you. But even so, I've been like a temporary safe place for you in the lands where you've gone. I'm going to gather you back from all those countries and give you the land of Israel back. You'll come home and do a total clean-up, throwing out all the nasty idols and disgusting images. I'll give you a brand new heart and put a new spirit in you. I'll do surgery on you—take out that heart of stone and give you a real, living heart. Then you'll actually follow my rules and be careful to do what I say. You'll be my people, and I'll be your God!
"‘But for those who are stubborn and can't get enough of their gross idols? I'll make sure they get exactly what they deserve for what they've done.’ This is the decree of the Master, God."

Then the cherubim lifted their wings, the wheels right beside them, and the Glory of the God of Israel was shining over them. The Glory of God rose up from the city and stopped on the mountain east of it.

Then, still in this vision from God's Spirit, the Spirit picked me up and carried me all the way back to the exiles in Babylon. And just like that, the vision was over. I told the exiles everything God had shown me.

title: My Life as a Meme: The Escape Plan
paragraphs: God's message hit my line: 'Yo, son of man, you're living with a crew that's straight-up rebellious. They've got eyes but are basically blind, and ears but they don't hear a thing. Total rebels. So, here's the plan: pack a duffel bag like you're getting kicked out. Do it in broad daylight so everyone sees you, and just walk away like you're being exiled. Maybe then they'll finally get what's happening, even though they're such rebels. Grab your stuff while they're all watching—just the essentials, like someone forced to leave home. When evening hits, head out like a real exile. While they're watching, I want you to dig a hole through the wall of your house and carry your bag through it. With everyone's eyes on you, throw the bag on your shoulder and walk off into the night. Cover your face so you don't have to see the place you'll never see again. I'm making you a living, breathing object lesson for the family of Israel.'

So, I did exactly what he told me to. I got my stuff, brought it out to the street for everyone to see, packed it up like an exile's go-bag, and then, when the sun started to set, I literally dug a hole through my house's wall with my bare hands. When it got dark, with everyone still staring, I bounced, throwing my bag over my shoulder.

The next morning, God hit me up again: 'Son of man, when someone from Israel, that rebellious crew, asks you, 'Bro, what are you even doing?' you tell them, 'The big boss, God, says this message is a direct @ to the prince in Jerusalem—we're talking about Zedekiah—but it's also for everyone in Israel.'
'Also, tell them, 'I'm literally acting out what's going to happen to you. What I'm doing now is a preview of what's coming for all the people of Israel. They're going into exile as prisoners.'

'The prince himself is gonna sling his bag over his shoulder in the dark and leave. He'll dig through the wall of his house, covering his face so he doesn't have to see the land he's leaving for good. But I'll make sure he gets caught and dragged to Babylon. He'll be blinded and will never see that land where he's gonna die. I'll scatter everyone who helped him escape, and his whole army, to the four winds, and tons of them will die in battle. They'll finally realize that I am God when I scatter them all over the world.'

'I'll let a few of them survive the fighting, the famine, and the plagues, but only so they can go and tell all the foreign nations about the disgusting stuff they've been up to. Then they will know that I am God.'

God's message came to me again: 'Son of man, when you eat, act like you're shaking with anxiety. When you drink, be all shaky and scared. Then tell the people of this land, everyone in Jerusalem and Israel, God's message: 'You're going to eat your food shaking with fear and drink your water in total terror, because your whole country is going to be wrecked as payback for all the messed-up stuff you've done. All the towns and cities will be ghost towns, and the fields will be destroyed. Then you'll realize that I am God.'
God's message came to me: 'Son of man, what's this little saying that's going around in Israel? 'Time keeps passing, but none of the prophecies ever come true.'?
'Tell them, 'God, the Master, says, That little saying is about to be canceled.'

'Tell them, 'Time's up. Every single warning is about to become reality. All the fake-deep prophecies and feel-good sermons are over for Israel. I, God, am speaking now. And what I say, goes. Nothing I say is getting delayed. What I say, I'll do—and it's happening soon, you rebels!' That's a decree from God, the Master.'

God's message came to me: 'Son of man, are you hearing what the people of Israel are saying? They're like, 'Oh, that prophet's warnings are for, like, way in the future.' Well, tell them, 'God, the Master, says, 'Nothing I say is on hold. What I say, happens. Period.' That's a decree from God, the Master.'

title: Calling Out the FAKE Prophets
paragraphs: God's message hit me: 'Son of man, you gotta call out the prophets of Israel. They're just making stuff up and calling it prophecy.'

'Preach the real deal to them. Tell them, \'Listen to God's actual message!\' The big boss, God, is calling out these clueless prophets who are just doing their own thing and have no idea what's really going on. Your prophets, Israel, are like jackals picking through trash. They haven't done a single thing to fix the city's problems and haven't risked anything to help Israel when judgment day comes. All they do is sell comforting fantasies and preach straight-up lies. They say \'God says...\' when God hasn't even thought about them. And they're just standing there, thinking their words actually mean something.

'Haven't you been selling total nonsense? Aren't your sermons just a bunch of lies, saying \'God says...\' when I haven't said a thing? So, listen up—this is a message from the Master, God—I'm so done with prophets who pass off their own ideas as visions and use their sermons to lie. I'm kicking them out of my people's council, deleting them from Israel's contacts, and blocking them from the land of Israel. Then you'll know that I am the real deal, God, the Master.

'The truth is, they've lied to my people. They've been saying, \'No worries, everything's fine,\' when it's totally not fine. When people build a flimsy wall, these prophets are right there, slapping on a coat of paint to make it look good. So tell those painters, \'When a massive storm hits with hailstones and a hurricane, and the wall comes crashing down, what good was that paint job you were so proud of?\'

'And that's for real what's gonna happen. I, God, the Master, am saying it: \'I'm about to unleash a hurricane of my anger, a storm of hailstones. I'll demolish that wall you covered in paint. I'll knock it flat to the ground, leaving only the foundation. And you'll all be goners in the rubble. Then you'll finally get that I am God.

'I'm going to unleash my fury on that wall and on everyone who plastered it. I'll tell them, \'The wall is gone, and so are the people who painted it—those so-called prophets of Israel who preached to Jerusalem, promising everything was fine when it was all about to fall apart. That's a decree from God, the Master.\'

'And the women prophets—son of man, you need to confront them too. These women are also just making things up. Stand up to them. Tell them \'You're doomed!\'—these women who make magic bracelets and custom head scarves, trying to trap people's souls. Say to them, \'Are you really going to destroy my people's souls and use them just to get rich and famous? You've disrespected me among my own people just to get ahead, using my name to make yourselves look good—killing souls that should have lived and protecting souls that should have died. You've been lying to people who just love to hear lies.\'

'So God says, \'I'm against all your little tricks and schemes you use to hunt down souls. I'm going to snatch them right out of your hands. I'll set free the souls you're trying to trap. I'll tear your magic bracelets and scarves to pieces and rescue my people from your grip so they're not your victims anymore. That's how you'll learn that I am God.

'Because you've confused good, innocent people with your lies, and you've made it easy for bad people to keep doing wrong, so it wouldn't even cross their minds to turn to me so I could save them, you're done. No more selling delusions, no more lying sermons. I'm rescuing my people from your clutches. And you'll realize that I am God.\'

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: So, some of Israel's leaders came to chill with me. Then, boom, God's message dropped: "Son of Man, these people have basically set up idols in their hearts. They're obsessed with stuff that's gonna totally ruin them. So why should I even listen to what they have to say? Tell them the Lord GOD's message is this: Any Israelite who's all about idols and into the sin that will wreck them, but still has the nerve to come to a prophet, needs to know this: I, GOD, will personally give them the answer they deserve, right along with their whole squad of idols. I'm about to get real with the hearts of the people of Israel, since they've all ditched me for their idols."

"So, tell the house of Israel: 'The Lord GOD says, Repent! Turn your back on your fake idols. Ditch all your gross habits. This goes for every single person in Israel, and even the foreigners living there—anyone who turns away from me, gets obsessed with idols, and puts wickedness on a pedestal in their life, and then still has the audacity to ask a prophet for my opinion—I, GOD, will step in and answer them myself. I'll go right up against them, make an example out of them—a total warning—and cut them off so you'll know that I am GOD.

"'And if a prophet gets tricked and gives these idol-lovers the false visions they want to hear, I, GOD, am the one who allowed that prophet to be deceived. But he's not getting away with it. I'll grab him and kick him out of my people. They'll both be guilty, the prophet and the person who asked him. This is so the house of Israel will never wander away from me again or get dirty with their rebellious ways. Instead, they'll be my people, and I will be their God. That's the deal from the Lord GOD.'"

God's message came to me again: "Son of Man, if a country sins against me by being unfaithful, and I have to step in and cut off their food supply with a famine, wiping out people and animals, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job—the ultimate big three—were there, it wouldn't save anyone else. Their own righteousness would only save themselves." This is the decree of the Lord GOD.

"Or, what if I sent wild animals to tear through the country, making it so deserted that no one would even dare to go through it? Even if those three guys were living there, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't even save their own sons or daughters. Only the three of them would be saved, and the country would become a wasteland.

"Or, what if I brought war on that country and was like, 'Let the swords go crazy!' killing people and animals? Even if those three were there, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't save their sons or daughters. Only they would be rescued.

"Or, if I sent a deadly plague on that country, pouring out my fury and killing both people and animals, and Noah, Daniel, and Job were alive, as surely as I am the living God, they couldn't save a single son or daughter. Only those three would be delivered because they were righteous.

"So here's the deal," says the Lord GOD, "when I send my four terrible judgments on Jerusalem—war, famine, wild animals, and disease—to wipe out people and animals. But check this out, believe it or not, there will be survivors. Some of their sons and daughters will make it out. When they come to you and you see the messed-up lives they were saved from, you'll get why I had to bring such a harsh judgment on Jerusalem. It was necessary. Yeah, when you see how they were living, you'll feel better about it. You'll understand the reason for everything I did in Jerusalem." This is the decree of the Lord GOD.

title: Useless Vine Gets Burned
paragraphs: Listen up. God hit me with this message: "For real, how does a grapevine's wood stack up against any random tree branch in the forest? You ever see anyone build something with vine wood? Or use it to make a peg to hang stuff on?

Yeah, I didn't think so. It's basically only good for firewood. And get this: it's just a flimsy piece of vine, you toss it in the fire, and then pull it out. The ends are burnt to a crisp and the middle is all charred. Is it good for anything now?
Hardly. It wasn't good for anything when it was whole, and being half-burnt is definitely not an upgrade. So what's it even good for?

So here's the message from God, the Master: Just like I chose that vine wood from all the other trees in the forest just to use as fuel for the fire, that's exactly how I'm gonna treat the people living in Jerusalem. I'm dead set against them. Even though they escaped the fire once, all charred and messed up, the fire's gonna totally consume them this time. When I make my stand against them, you'll know without a doubt that I am God. I'm going to turn this country into a total wasteland because they've been so unfaithful." That's the final word from God, the Master.

title: Jerusalem's Glow-Up & Ghosting God: A Wild Story
paragraphs: God's message hit me up. He said, "Yo, son of man, you need to call out Jerusalem for all the wild stuff she's been doing. Tell her this is what the LORD God has to say: 'Jerusalem, your roots are in Canaan. Your dad was an Amorite and your mom was a Hittite.'

'Back on the day you were born, nobody even bothered to cut your umbilical cord. You weren't washed, nobody rubbed you with salt—which was a thing back then—or even wrapped you in a blanket. Literally no one cared about you. Not a single person did anything to show you some love. You were just tossed out in a field, all dirty and unwanted—a literal newborn nobody wanted.

'Then I came walking by. I saw you there, a total mess, all bloody and helpless. And I said to you, lying there in your own filth, "Live! And grow up, like a flower in the field." And you did. You grew up, got tall, and became a woman, with a full chest and long hair. But you were still totally naked and vulnerable, just out there and exposed.

'So I came by again and saw you were ready for love. I took you under my wing, gave you clothes, and kept you safe. I promised to love you and we got married—a covenant. I, the LORD God, gave you my word. You became mine. I gave you a good bath, washed off all that old blood, and put some nice-smelling oils on you. I hooked you up with a colorful dress and some leather sandals. I gave you linen shirts and a whole wardrobe of expensive clothes. I decked you out in jewelry: bracelets, a necklace, emerald rings, sapphire earrings, and a diamond crown. You had all the best and most beautiful things: amazing clothes and gourmet food, with honey and oil. You were drop-dead gorgeous. A queen! You got famous worldwide, a legendary beauty, all because of the beauty I gave you. That's a decree from the LORD God.

'But all that beauty went straight to your head. You used your fame to become an immoral woman, just grabbing any guy who walked by and sleeping with him. You took the nice clothes I gave you and made little pagan shrine-tents out of them, turning them into brothels. That kind of thing should never, ever happen.

'And then you took the beautiful jewelry I gave you, my gold and my silver, and you made these gross male idols for your shrines. You decorated your beds with fancy silks and used my special oils and incense to make them smell good. Then you took the amazing food I gave you—the fresh bread, fruit, and all the good spices—and you served it up like a fancy meal in your pagan shrines. That's what you did, says the LORD God.

'And then you took your own sons and daughters—the children you had for me—and you killed them. You sacrificed them to your idols. Like, wasn't being unfaithful bad enough? Now you're a murderer, too, killing my kids and offering them up to idols.
'Not one time during all these years of your disgusting, obscene cheating did you even think about where you came from—how you were a naked, bloody, abandoned newborn.

'And then, to top off all your evil, you built your flashy brothels in every single town square. You are so doomed! says the LORD God. You set up shop on every major street corner, selling your body and spreading your legs for anyone who passed by.

'Then you took your business international. You started sleeping with the Egyptians, joining in on their crazy pagan rituals. The more you slept around, the angrier I got. Finally, I had to step in. I shrank your territory and let your enemies walk all over you. Even the Philistine women—and this is wild—were shocked by how unfaithful you were acting.

'But you didn't stop there. You went after the Assyrians. Your appetite was just endless. But you still weren't satisfied. So you hooked up with the Babylonians, a whole country of traders, and you still weren't satisfied.

'Man, your soul is so sick! You did all this stuff—you're like the world champion of unfaithful ones! You built your brothels on every corner and in every neighborhood, but you were different from a regular unfaithful one because you refused to get paid.

'Wives who cheat on their husbands get gifts from their lovers. And guys usually pay prostitutes. But you pay your lovers! You bribe guys from all over to come sleep with you! You're the total opposite of a normal woman of the streets who gets paid for sex. You're paying guys for it! You've somehow made being unfaithful even more messed up!

'So, you unfaithful one, listen to God's message: The LORD God says, because you were so shameless in your cheating, stripping down for every lover, and because of your gross idols and all the children you murdered for them, I'm going to get all your lovers together—the ones you liked and the ones you hated. I'm gonna gather them all around you like a jury. And I'm gonna strip you naked in front of them, so they can all see the real you. Then I'm gonna sentence you like an adulterous, murderous woman. I'm gonna give you a taste of my fury!

'I'm gonna hand you over to your lovers. They're gonna tear down your brothels and pagan shrines. They'll rip your clothes off, steal your jewelry, and leave you naked and exposed. Then they'll call a big meeting, and a mob will stone you and chop you up with swords. They'll burn down your houses. It's gonna be a huge public judgment—with all the other women watching!
'And that's how I'll put a stop to your life of whoring. No more paying guys to sleep with you! By then, my anger will be gone. My jealousy will chill out.

'Because you forgot what it was like when you were young and just kept making me mad with all your behavior, I'm gonna make you pay for it. Didn't you just keep making your disgusting sins worse and worse with your unfaithful ways?

'You know that saying, "Like mother, like daughter"? Everyone's gonna use that about you. You're just like your mother, who couldn't stand her husband and kids. And you're just like your sisters, who couldn't stand their husbands and kids. Your mother was a Hittite and your father was an Amorite.

'Your older sister is Samaria, who lived north of you with her daughters. Your younger sister is Sodom, who lived south of you with her daughters. And didn't you act just like them? Didn't you do the same disgusting things they did? Actually, it didn't take you long to get even worse than them! As sure as I am the living God, says the LORD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did anything close to as bad as what you and your daughters have done.

'Your sister Sodom's sin was this: She and her daughters were living in total luxury—they were proud, ate way too much, and were super lazy. They didn't care about the poor and oppressed. They were arrogant and lived disgusting lives. And you know what I did? I got rid of them.

'And Samaria? She didn't even sin half as much as you. You've done way more obscene things than she ever did. You make your two sisters look good by comparison! Seriously, they look like saints next to you. Because you've out-sinned them so badly, you've actually made them look righteous. Aren't you ashamed? Well, you're gonna have to live with it. You'll go down in history as the one who out-sinned her two sisters!

'But I'm going to turn their fortunes around—Sodom's and Samaria's. And guess what? I'll turn your fortune around right along with them! Still, you're going to have to live with your shame. And by accepting your shame, you'll actually make your two sisters feel a little better. Your sisters, Sodom and Samaria, will go back to how they were before, and you'll go back to how you were before. Remember when you were so arrogant, acting all high and mighty, looking down on your sister Sodom? That was before your own evil was exposed. Now you're the one everyone makes fun of—the Edomite women, the Philistine women, and everyone around. You just have to deal with it, accept the shame of your disgusting and vile life. That's a decree from the LORD God.

'The LORD God says, I'm going to do to you exactly what you did. You treated my promise like it was nothing and broke our covenant. But still, I'll remember the covenant I made with you when you were young, and I'll make a new, everlasting covenant with you. You'll remember your messed-up past and feel true regret when you get your sisters back, both the older and the younger one. I'll give them to you as daughters, but they won't be part of your covenant. I'll establish my covenant with you, and you'll know that I am God. You'll remember your past and be so ashamed, but when I forgive you for everything you've done, it will leave you speechless.' That's the decree of the LORD God."

title: Two Eagles, One Vine, and a Whole Lotta Drama
paragraphs: God's message hit me up. He said, "Son of man, drop a riddle for the house of Israel. Tell them a story. Say, 'The Lord, the Master, says:

'A huge eagle, like, massive wingspan, crazy long feathers, super colorful and bright, flew over to Lebanon. It snapped the top right off a cedar tree, broke off the top branch, and carried it off to this land full of business people, dropping it in a city of shopkeepers. Then it took a cutting from the land and planted it in some really good, well-watered soil, like you'd plant a willow by a river. It sprouted and grew into this awesome vine, but it stayed low to the ground. Its branches reached up toward the eagle, and its roots got super established—a legit vine with shoots and branches popping out.

'Then another huge eagle showed up, also with a massive wingspan and thick feathers. And this vine, from where it was planted, started sending its roots out toward the new eagle. Its branches stretched out, trying to get water from him, even from far away. It was planted in good, rich soil, and it was supposed to grow branches, produce fruit, and become this noble, amazing vine.

'The Lord, the Master, asks, Is this thing really going to thrive? Won't the first eagle just rip it up by the roots, leave its fruit to rot, and all its branches to shrivel up into a dead, withered vine? It wouldn't even take much effort or a big crew to pull it up. And even if it gets moved, will it do well? When that hot east wind hits it, won't it just shrivel up? Won't it just dry up and blow away from the very spot where it was planted?'
God's message came to me again: "Go tell these rebels, 'Do you even get it? Do you have any clue what this means?'

"Tell them, 'The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and leaders, and brought them back to Babylon. He took a guy from the royal family, made a deal with him, and made him swear loyalty. The king of Babylon took all the top dogs into exile to make sure this kingdom stayed weak—so it wouldn't get any big ideas—and so it would keep the deal with him to even have a future.

"'But what did he do? He rebelled. He sent his people to Egypt to try and get horses and a huge army. You think that's gonna work? You think he's gonna get away with that? Does anyone just break a promise like that and get off scot-free?

"'As sure as I'm the living God, this king who broke his promise and his deal will die in that country, in Babylon. And Pharaoh, with his big army and all those soldiers, won't lift a finger to help him when Babylon attacks the city and wipes everyone out. Because he broke his word and the covenant, even after giving his solemn promise, and because he went and did all this stuff anyway, he's not getting away.

"'So, the Lord, the Master, says, As sure as I am the living God, because the king dissed my oath and broke my covenant, I'm gonna make the consequences crash down on his head. I'll send a search party for him and catch him. I'll take him to Babylon and put him on trial for completely disrespecting me. All his best soldiers and the rest of the army will be killed in battle, and anyone who's left will be scattered everywhere. Then you'll know that I, God, have spoken.

"'The Lord, the Master, says, But I'm personally going to take a shoot from the very top of that tall cedar, a cutting from the crown of the tree, and I'll plant it on a high and majestic mountain, on the high mountain of Israel. It will grow, putting out branches and fruit—a truly majestic cedar. All kinds of birds will come and live under it. They'll build nests in the shade of its branches. Then all the trees in the field will know that I, God, am the one who makes the big tree small and the small tree big, who makes the green tree dry up and the dry tree sprout green branches. I, God, said it—and I'll do it.'"

title: Your Choices, Your Consequences
paragraphs: God's message came to me, and he was like, 'What's with this saying everyone keeps repeating all over the country? 'The parents ate sour grapes, and the kids are the ones with the stomachache.'

'For real, as I live and breathe,' says God, 'you're not going to be using that saying in Israel anymore. Every single person—man, woman, child—is mine. The parent and the kid, both belong to me. You die for your own screw-ups, not someone else's.'

'Picture this: a guy who lives a good life, treats people right, and keeps his relationships solid. He doesn't join in on pagan worship, doesn't get into all the idol stuff that's so popular in Israel, doesn't try to get with his neighbor's wife, doesn't sleep around, doesn't push people around, doesn't get into crazy debt, doesn't steal, always helps out the hungry and gives clothes to those who need them, doesn't take advantage of the poor, isn't driven by greed, and treats everyone the same. He follows my rules and sticks to my laws. This guy, who lives right, will have a full and real life. That's a promise from God, the boss.'

'But what if this guy has a kid who's a total mess—violent, a murderer, and does all the things the dad never did? He's all about the pagan shrines, goes after his neighbor's wife, bullies the weak, steals, racks up debt, is obsessed with idols, does some seriously messed-up stuff, and takes advantage of the poor. You think this kid is gonna live? No way. He's done all this terrible stuff, so he's going to die, and it'll be his own fault.'

'Now, let's say that kid has a son who sees all the messed-up things his dad did. He sees it, but he doesn't follow in his dad's footsteps. He doesn't get into pagan worship, doesn't care about the popular idols, doesn't try to get with his neighbor's wife, doesn't bully anyone, is willing to help people out, doesn't steal, always gives food to the hungry and clothes to those who need them, isn't greedy, and doesn't take advantage of the poor. He does what I say, follows my laws, and lives by my rules. This person won't die for his dad's mistakes; he'll live a good life. But the dad will die for what he did—for hurting the weak, robbing people, and doing what's totally wrong.'

'Are you seriously asking, 'So why doesn't the kid have to pay for his dad's mistakes?' Isn't it obvious? It's because the kid did what was right. Since he was careful to do what was right and fair, he'll live a good life. The person who messes up is the one who dies. The kid doesn't get blamed for the parent's mistakes, and the parent doesn't get blamed for the kid's. If you live a good life, you get the credit; if you live a bad life, you're the one who's guilty.'

'But if a bad person turns away from their messed-up life and starts following all my rules, living a good and fair life, they'll live. For real, they won't die. I'm not going to hold on to a list of all their past mistakes. They will live. Do you think I like it when bad people die? No, what I really want is for them to turn their lives around and start living right—really living.'

'The same goes for a good person who turns their back on a good life and starts messing up, doing the same terrible things that bad people do. You think they're going to live? I don't keep a record of all the good things they did, like a bank account they can just draw from. Because they turned their back on me and piled up all that bad stuff, they'll die.'

'Are you really saying, 'That's not fair! God's not fair!'? Listen up, Israel. You think I'm not fair? You're the ones who aren't being fair! If a good person turns away from their good life and starts doing bad things, they'll die for it. They'll die for their own mistakes. And if a bad person turns away from their bad life and starts living a good and fair life, they'll save their life. Because they owned up to all the wrong they did and left it behind, they will live. For real, they won't die.'
'And yet, Israel keeps complaining, 'That's not fair! God's not fair.' You think I'm not fair, Israel? You're the ones who aren't fair.'

'So here's the deal, Israel: I'm going to judge each of you based on how you live. So turn your life around! Stop being rebellious so your mistakes don't drag you down. Clean up your act. No more rebelling, please. Get a new heart! Get a new spirit! Why would you choose to die, Israel? I don't get any pleasure from anyone's death. That's a promise from God, the boss. So make a clean break! Live!'

title: Royalty to Ruin: A Sad Song for Israel's Princes
paragraphs: Go ahead and sing a sad song for the leaders of Israel. It goes like this:

Man, your mom was like this total boss lioness. She hung out with a whole crew of lions, and her cubs got super strong. She raised one of them to be this absolute unit of a lion. He learned to hunt and he started hunting people. Other countries freaked out and set a trap. They caught him, put hooks in him, and dragged him all the way to Egypt.

So when the momma lion realized her first son was a lost cause, she was like, 'Alright, bet.' She took her other cub and trained him up to be another beast. He rolled with the other lions, learned to hunt, and yeah, he hunted people too. This dude went on a rampage, wrecking their towns and leaving them in shambles. The whole country was shook by his roar. So, all the nations teamed up to take him down. They set traps and finally caught him. They slapped a wooden collar on him and shipped him off to the king of Babylon. You wouldn't hear his roar in the mountains of Israel ever again.

Okay, let me put it another way. Your mom was like a grapevine planted by a river, totally thriving with tons of branches and grapes because it had all the water it needed. It grew these super strong branches, the kind you could make a king's scepter from. It grew so tall it was basically touching the clouds. Its branches were everywhere, and everyone could see it. But then, someone got mad, ripped it out of the ground, and just threw it down. A hot wind came and dried it all up, stripping off all its fruit. Those strong branches got so dry they were only good for firewood. Now it's just a dead stick in the middle of a desert, totally useless except for starting a campfire. There's no trace of those awesome branches that could've been a royal scepter.
(This is a sad song, the kind you sing when you've got the blues.)

title: God Spills the Tea on Israel's Messy History
paragraphs: So, get this. It was the seventh year, fifth month, tenth day. Some of Israel's leaders came to get some advice from God, and they were just sitting there in front of me.

Then God's message hit me: "Son of man, go talk to the leaders of Israel. Tell them, 'God, the Master, is saying this: You came to ask me questions? For real? As long as I'm alive, I'm not dealing with questions from you. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"
"Son of man, why don't you just do it? Yeah, go on. Call them out. Confront them with the totally messed-up stuff their ancestors did. Tell them that God, the Master, says:

"'The day I chose Israel, I revealed myself to them in Egypt. I made a huge, solemn promise to Jacob's descendants, saying, 'I am God, *your* personal God.' That same day, I swore I'd get them out of Egypt and bring them to a land I had scouted out just for them—a land flowing with milk and honey, like, the best place ever.
"'Back then, I told them, 'Get rid of all the gross things you're obsessed with. Don't get yourselves all dirty with those fake Egyptian gods. I'm the only God, your God.'

"'But they totally rebelled against me and wouldn't listen to a single thing I said. Nobody got rid of the nasty stuff they were addicted to. They clung to Egypt's fake gods like their lives depended on it. I was *this* close to unleashing my anger on them right there in Egypt. But then I chilled out. I acted based on who I am, not how I felt. I did it in a way that would get me respect, not hate, from the nations around them who saw me reveal myself by promising to lead my people out of Egypt. And then I did it: I led them out of Egypt and into the desert.

"'I gave them rules to live by, showed them how to live a good life by listening to me. I also gave them my weekly holy rest days, my 'Sabbaths,' which were like a sign between me and them to show them that I, God, am the one making them holy.

"'But Israel rebelled against me in the desert. They didn't follow my rules. They hated my laws for living a good and obedient life. And they completely disrespected my holy Sabbaths. I seriously thought about just letting all my anger out on them right there in the desert. But I took a breath and acted based on my character, not my feelings, so the other nations who saw me bring them out would respect me, not trash-talk me. But I did make a serious promise in the desert that I wouldn't bring them into that amazing land flowing with milk and honey that I had picked for them. I took back my promise because they hated my laws, wouldn't follow my rules, and kept disrespecting my holy Sabbaths. They'd rather live by their fake idol gods. But I didn't go all the way; I didn't completely wipe them out in the desert.

"'Then I talked to their kids in the desert: 'Don't be like your parents. Don't follow their ways. Don't get yourselves dirty with their fake gods. I am God, your God. Follow my rules and live by my laws. Keep my Sabbaths as holy rest days, signs between us that I am God, your God.'

"'But the kids rebelled against me too. They didn't follow my rules or keep my laws for living right. And they disrespected my Sabbaths. I was so ready to just dump my anger on them, right there in the desert. But again, I held back. I acted based on who I am, not how I felt, so the nations who saw me bring them out would honor me.

"'But I did make a solemn promise in the desert. I swore I'd scatter them all over the world, sending them everywhere because they didn't keep my laws or live by my statutes. They disrespected my Sabbaths and were still addicted to their parents' fake gods. Since they were so set on living bad lives, I gave them rules that were no good and laws that couldn't lead to life. I just left them to it. They got filthy, and in a twisted move, they sacrificed their firstborn kids in the fire. The horror of that should have been a wake-up call for them to realize that I am God.'

"So, son of man, speak to Israel. Tell them God says, 'And if that wasn't bad enough, your ancestors insulted me even more by betraying me. When I brought them into the land I had promised to give them, every time they saw a hill with some sketchy sex-and-religion shrine or a bunch of trees where pagan temple workers did their thing, they were there, all in on the pagan stuff. I asked them, 'What's this hill you keep going to?'' (It's still called 'Pagan Hills' today, btw.)

"So, say to Israel, 'This is the message from God, the Master: You're messing up your lives by copying your parents. By repeating their disgusting habits, you've become just like them. By burning your kids as sacrifices, you've become as filthy as your fake gods—even today!
"'And you think I'm going to answer questions from people like you, Israel? As sure as I am the living God, I, God, the Master, refuse to be questioned by you!
"'And that little thought you're having? It's never gonna happen. You're thinking, 'We'll just be like everyone else, like the other nations. We'll worship gods we can make and control.'

"'As sure as I am the living God, says God, the Master, think again! With a huge show of strength and a terrifying wave of anger, I will be your King! I'll bring you back from the nations, gather you from all the countries where you've been scattered, with my power and my anger. I'll bring you to the 'desert of nations' and put you on trial, face-to-face with my judgment.

"'Just like I judged your ancestors in the desert of Egypt, I'm going to judge you. I'll check out every single person as you come, and I'll bring you into the covenant. I'll kick out the rebels and traitors. I'll lead them out of exile, but they're not coming back to Israel.
"'Then you'll finally get that I am God.

"'But as for you, people of Israel, this is the message from God, the Master: Go on, serve your fake idols! But later, you'll change your minds and stop disrespecting me with your pagan gifts and fake gods. Because on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, I, God, the Master, declare that the entire nation of Israel will worship me. I'll welcome them there with open arms. I'll expect your best gifts and offerings, all your holy sacrifices. What's more, I'll receive you as the best kind of offering when I bring you back from all the lands where you've been scattered. I'll show the whole world that I am The Holy One. When I bring you back to the land of Israel, the land I solemnly promised to your ancestors, you'll realize that I am God. Then and there you'll remember everything you've done, the way you lived that made you so filthy—and you'll be disgusted with yourselves.

"'But, dear Israel, you'll also realize that I am God when I deal with you based on who I am, not based on the evil lives you've lived and the corrupt history you've made. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"
God's message came to me: "Son of man, face south. Let the message flow out against the south. Prophesy against the wilderness forest of the south.

"Tell the forest of the south, 'Listen to God's message! God, the Master, says, I'm going to start a fire in you that will burn up every single tree, the dead ones and the live ones. No one will be able to put out the fire. The whole country from south to north will be scorched by it. Everyone's going to see that I, God, started the fire and it's not going out.'"
And I was like, "Oh, God, everyone is saying I just make up stories."

title: God's Sword Is Coming for EVERYONE
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up: “Yo, Son of Man, face Jerusalem and just let this message flow out against the Sanctuary. Prophesy against Israel and tell them, ‘God’s message is here: I’m actually against you. I’m pulling my sword out, and it’s the end for everyone—the good and the bad. And because I’m not playing favorites, my sword is gonna be felt by everyone from the south to the north. The whole world will know I’m not messing around.’
“So you gotta start groaning. Like, double over in pain and make a huge scene!

“When they ask you, ‘Bro, why are you groaning and making such a fuss?’ you tell them, ‘Because of the news that’s about to drop. It’s gonna leave everyone speechless. Hearts will literally stop, and knees will turn to jelly. For real, it’s coming. There’s no stopping it. That’s a decree from the Lord GOD himself.’”
God’s message came to me again: “Son of Man, prophesy. Tell them, ‘The Lord says this:
“‘A sword! A sword! It’s razor-sharp and polished, sharpened to kill, and polished to flash like lightning!
“‘My kid, you totally disrespected the royal authority of Judah by bowing down to every fake idol out there.
“‘This sword is made to shine, to be held and swung. It’s sharpened and polished, all ready for the killer to go to work.’
“So scream and wail, Son of Man. This sword is coming for my own people! The leaders of Israel and my people—they’re all being left for the sword to deal with! So just freak out! Tear your hair out!
“‘A test is coming. So why did you brush off discipline? You can’t just ignore it. This is a decree from the Lord GOD.’

“So, prophesy, Son of Man! Clap your hands. Get their attention. Tell them the sword is coming down—once, twice, even three times. It’s a sword for a total massacre, a relentless sword you can’t escape. People will be dropping left and right like dominoes. I’ve put a deadly sword at every city gate, flashing like lightning, ready to kill. Go right, slash left, you deadly, sharp-edged sword! Then I’ll clap my hands too, as a sign that my anger is finally done. I, GOD, have said it.”

God’s message came to me: “Son of Man, map out two roads for the king of Babylon’s sword to take. They both start from the same place. Put a signpost where the roads split. One sign points the way for the sword to Rabbah of the Ammonites. The other sign points to Judah and the fortress of Jerusalem. The king of Babylon is standing at that fork in the road, trying to figure out which way to go using magic. He’s drawing straws, rolling some kind of god-dice, and checking out a goat’s liver. He looks at his right hand: the sign says, ‘Go for Jerusalem!’ So now he’s on his way with battering rams, ready to kill, shouting battle cries, breaking down city gates, and building siege ramps.
“To the leaders of Judah, who made their own promises, this will seem like a bogus prediction. But he’s going to call them out on their guilt, and they’re all going to be captured.
“So this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because your sin is now completely exposed for everyone to see, you’re going to be taken captive.

“‘And you, Zedekiah, you blasphemous and evil prince of Israel: your time is up. It’s punishment payday. God says, take off your royal crown. Business as usual is over. The underdog is getting a promotion, and the top dog is getting demoted. Ruins, ruins, ruins! I’m turning this whole place into ruins. And it’ll stay that way until the one who has the right to it comes. Then I’ll give it to him.’
“But, Son of Man, your job is to prophesy. Tell them, ‘This is the message from the Lord GOD against the Ammonites and their cruel trash talk:

“‘A sword! A sword! Pulled out to kill, sharp as a razor, flashing like lightning. Even though there are all these false visions about the sword going around in Ammon, it’s still coming to slice the necks of the Ammonites, because it’s their punishment payday. Put the sword back! I’m going to judge you right in your own homeland, where you grew up. I’ll pour out my anger on you, breathing fire down your neck. I’ll hand you over to brutal men who are experts in torture. You’ll end up as firewood. Your country will be littered with dead bodies. No one will even remember you. I, GOD, have spoken.’”

title: God Calls Out the Whole City (It's Bad)
paragraphs: God's message hit me up, and it was like, "Yo, son of man, are you gonna call out this messed-up, violent city or not? C'mon, are you gonna judge it? Then do it. You gotta confront them with all the wild stuff they're doing. Tell them, 'This is what God, the Master, is saying: You're a city that's murderous deep down, just asking for trouble. You're obsessed with fake gods, making yourselves totally gross. With all your killing, you've racked up some serious guilt. With all your idol-making, you've just gotten filthy. You've basically hit the self-destruct button on your own existence. I'm gonna put you on display as a total joke to the world, the biggest laughingstock. People from all over will make fun of you for being so nasty and chaotic.'"

"Your leaders, the princes of Israel right there with you, are all trying to outdo each other in crime. Your whole community disrespects parents, treats foreigners like trash, and bullies orphans and widows. You couldn't care less about my holy things and you totally ignore my Sabbaths. You've got people spreading lies and causing bloodshed, running to the hills for these weird pagan rituals and just going wild. Incest is a thing now. Guys are forcing themselves on women whenever they want. It's total chaos when it comes to sex. It's a free-for-all: your neighbor, your daughter-in-law, your own sister. You can even hire someone to kill for you, charging insane interest is normal, and ripping people off is just another Tuesday.
"'And you've completely forgotten about me. That's a decree from God, the Master.'

"'So look! I'm clapping my hands, like, 'Hello?!' to get your attention about all the greedy, violent stuff you're doing. You think you can handle what's coming? You think you'll be able to stand it when I start dealing with you?'

"'I, God, have said it. I'm gonna put a stop to this. I'm gonna scatter you everywhere, all over the world. I'm gonna force you to stop your disgusting lifestyle. You'll be humiliated, covered in your own filth for all the world to see. And then you'll finally get that I am God.'"

God's message came to me again: "Son of man, the people of Israel are like slag to me—you know, the useless gunk that's left over after you melt down good metals like copper, tin, iron, and lead. Just a worthless pile of junk. So tell them, 'God, the Master, has spoken: Because you've all become useless slag, I'm warning you: I'm gonna gather all of you in Jerusalem. Just like people throw silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into a super-hot furnace and blast it with fire to melt it all down, that's what I'm gonna do to you in my anger. I'll gather you up and melt you down. I'll blast you with the fire of my fury and melt you in the furnace. Just like silver melts, you'll be melted. That should get the message through. Then you'll know that I, God, have unleashed my anger on you.'"

God's message came to me: "Son of man, tell her, 'You're a land that got zero rain when I was angry with you, not even a little shower. The leaders among you got desperate, like roaring lions just killing whatever they see. They grabbed and stole everything, leaving a bunch of widows behind.'

"'Your priests totally ignored my law and disrespected my holy things. They act like there's no difference between what's sacred and what's not. They tell people that right and wrong are basically the same. They have zero respect for my holy Sabbaths, and they make me look bad by trying to drag me down to their level. Your politicians are like wolves, prowling around, killing, and greedily taking whatever they want. And your preachers? They just cover for the politicians, faking visions and special messages. They're like, 'This is what God, the Master, says...' when God hasn't said a single word. Extortion is everywhere, robbery is an epidemic, the poor and needy get abused, and outsiders are treated like dirt with no way to get justice.'

"'I looked for someone, anyone, who would stand up for me against all this, who would fix the city's defenses, who would take a stand in the gap to protect this land so I wouldn't have to destroy it.
