But I couldn't find a single person. Not one. So I'm gonna pour out my anger on them, burn them to a crisp with my hot fury, and make them face the consequences of everything they've done. That's a decree from God, the Master.'"

title: The Wild Story of Two Sisters & Their Bad Choices
paragraphs: God hit me up with a message: "Yo, son of man, listen up. There were these two sisters, same mom and everything. They started messing around way back when they were young in Egypt. Guys were all over them from the get-go. The older one was Oholah, and the younger one was Oholibah. They were mine, and they had kids.
Just so you know, Oholah is basically Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.

So Oholah, even though she was with me, started chasing other guys. She was obsessed with the Assyrians—these military dudes in sharp blue uniforms, important-looking officials, all handsome and riding fancy horses. She couldn't get enough. She went all in, sleeping with the top Assyrian guys and getting into all their idol worship stuff. She never quit the wild life she started back in Egypt, just kept sleeping around with anyone who'd give her attention.

So I was like, 'Fine, have it your way,' and let her go with the Assyrians she was so crazy about. They totally wrecked her life. They stripped her, took her kids, and then, the ultimate humiliation, they killed her. Her name basically became 'Shame'—a total cautionary tale.

Her sister Oholibah saw all this go down, but believe it or not, she got even crazier with her lust and wild living. She also went nuts for the Assyrians: all the big shots, the well-dressed soldiers on their awesome horses—the whole Assyrian elite. I saw she was getting just as messy. Both sisters were on the same track. But Oholibah took it to another level. When she saw carvings of Babylonian guys on the walls, all painted red, looking fly with fancy belts and turbans, all looking super important—famous Babylonians!—she went wild and sent them messages, inviting them over. The Babylonians came running, hooked up with her, and just made a mess of her life. After they completely used her, she got bored of them. Then she just put her whole messy life on blast for everyone to see.

I turned my back on her, just like I did with her sister. But that didn't stop her. She went even harder. She started thinking about her younger days, when she first started hooking up in Egypt. That just made her want even more intense, vulgar guys—like stallions who couldn't be controlled. She was nostalgic for the wildness of her youth in Egypt, where guys were all over her.

'So, Oholibah, this is the deal from God, the Master: I'm about to sic your old flames on you, the ones you got tired of and ghosted. I'm bringing them at you from all sides—the Babylonians, all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians. All those good-looking young guys, the officials and governors, the elite officers and celebs, all on their fancy horses. They're gonna roll up on you from the north, fully armed, with chariots and a massive army. I'm letting them be the judges. They'll punish you their way. I'll be against you, no holding back, as they tear you apart. They'll mutilate you, cutting off your ears and nose, and killing whoever's left. They'll take your kids as slaves, and anyone who survives will be burned. They'll rip off your clothes and steal your jewelry. I'm shutting down your whole wild lifestyle, the one you started in Egypt. You won't be looking back on it fondly anymore. You won't be daydreaming about Egypt.

'A message from God, the Master: I'm about to hand you over to the very people you hate, the ones who now disgust you. They'll treat you with pure hatred, leave you naked and exposed for everyone to see. Your whole lustful, messy life will be out in the open. Your own choices brought you here, because you chased after other nations and got dirty with their fake gods.
'You copied your sister's life. So now you're going to drink from the same cup she did.'
'This is the message from God, the Master:

'You're going to drink your sister's cup, and it's a cup as deep as a canyon and as wide as an ocean. You'll be made fun of and mocked as you drink it all down. You'll be blackout drunk, and you'll be crying your eyes out as you drink from that cup of pure terror. It's the cup of your sister, Samaria. You'll drink every last drop, then you'll smash it and eat the pieces, and end up tearing at your own body. I've said it—this is a decree from God, the Master.

'So, God, the Master, says: Because you completely forgot about me, pushed me to the side, you now have to face the consequences for what you've done—pay for your messy sex life and all your cheating.'"

Then God said to me, "Son of man, are you going to confront Oholah and Oholibah about what they've done? You need to make them face their insane behavior, from cheating to actual murder. They cheated on me with their fake idols, and then sacrificed the children they had with me to feed those idols! And that's not all. They also disrespected my holy Temple and my holy Sabbaths. On the exact same day they sacrificed their kids to idols, they walked right into my Temple and trashed it. That's what they did—in my own house!

"On top of that, they sent out special messengers to invite guys from far away—and of course, they came. The sisters got all dolled up, put on makeup and their finest clothes. They lounged on a fancy bed, with incense and oils burning—my incense and my oils! A whole crowd gathered, a rowdy, drunk mob. They put bracelets on the sisters' arms and crowns on their heads.

"I said, 'She's gotta be tired of this life!' but that didn't stop them. Guys kept showing up, day and night, like men chasing after an immoral woman. That's how they treated Oholah and Oholibah, these two worn-out women.
"Good people will judge them, sentencing them for adultery and murder. Because that's what their lives were about: adultery and murder."
"God says, 'Unleash a mob on them. Let them be terrorized and robbed! Let the mob stone them and chop them to pieces—kill all their children, burn down their houses!

"'I'm going to put an end to this kind of unfaithful behavior in this country, so that all women will get the message and not copy you. You'll pay the price for all your obsessive cheating. You'll pay in full for your affairs with idols. And then you'll finally realize that I am God, the Master.'"

title: God's CRAZY Stew Pot Prophecy
paragraphs: So, God's message hit me up in the ninth year, tenth month, and tenth day. He was like, 'Yo, son of man, you gotta write down today's date. The king of Babylon has surrounded Jerusalem, like, right now. And you need to tell this rebellious crew a story.'

'Get the stew pot out. Fill it up with water. Throw in some big chunks of meat, all the good stuff—we're talking loin and brisket. Grab the best bones from the best sheep you can find. Stack up a bunch of wood underneath, get that thing boiling, and let it cook.'
'The Lord God is saying this:
'It's over for the city of murderers, for that pot caked with so much gunk you can't even scrub it clean. Just dump out the pot, piece by piece. Don't even worry about who gets what.'

'The evidence of all the killing is all over the city. Blood is literally on the streets, and no one's even trying to clean it up. It's just out there for everyone to see, and it's seriously making me angry, like, ready to get my revenge.'
'So, this is what the Lord God says:

'It's over for the city of murderers! I'm gonna pile on the wood myself. Stack it high, light it up, cook the meat, season it, dump the broth, and then just burn the bones. Then I'll put the empty pot on the fire and heat it until it's glowing red-hot. That way the bronze will glow, all the germs will be killed, and all the nasty stuff will be burned off. But honestly, it's hopeless. It's too far gone. The gunk is just too thick.'

'Your caked-on filth is your disgusting lifestyle. I wanted to clean you up, but you wouldn't let me. So I'm not even gonna try to clean you anymore until my anger finally chills out. I, God, have said it, and I'm gonna do it. I'm not holding back. I have no more sympathy. I'm not changing my mind. You're getting exactly what you deserve. That's a decree from the Lord God.'

God's message came to me: 'Son of man, I'm about to take the delight of your life away from you—it's gonna be a huge blow, I know. But please, no crying. Keep your sadness to yourself. No public mourning. Just get dressed like normal and go to work—none of the usual funeral stuff.'
I preached to the people in the morning. That evening, my wife died. The next morning, I did exactly what I was told.
The people came up to me and were like, 'Tell us why you're acting like this. What's this all about?'

So I told them, 'God's word came to me, and he said, 'Tell the family of Israel, This is what the Lord God says: I'm going to destroy my own Sanctuary, the place you're so proud of, your impenetrable fort, the delight of your life, the thing your heart wants most. And the kids you left behind? They're going to be killed.'

'Then you'll do exactly what I've done. You won't do any of the usual funeral rituals. You'll get dressed like normal and go about your work. No tears. But your sins will eat you up from the inside, and you'll just groan to each other. Ezekiel will be your example. The way he did it is the way you'll do it.'
'When this happens, you'll finally get that I am the Lord God.'

'And you, son of man: on the day I take away the people's safe place, their great joy, the delight of their life, what they've wanted most, along with all their children—on that exact day, a survivor will show up and tell you what happened to the city. You'll break your silence and start talking again, talking to the survivor. Once again, you'll be an example for them. And they'll finally get that I am God.'

title: God's Payback on Israel's Haters
paragraphs: God's message hit me up:

"Yo, son of man, face the Ammonites and call them out. Tell them to listen up to the message from God, the Master. This is what God's gotta say: Since you were all hyped and cheering when my holy place got wrecked, when Judah's land was torn up, and when Israel's people were dragged off into exile, I'm handing you over to the people from the east. They're gonna roll in, set up camp, eat your food, and drink your milk. I'm turning your main city, Rabbah, into a camel pasture and your towns into sheep pens. Then you'll finally get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because you clapped and cheered, throwing all your nasty shade at the land of Israel, I'm about to step in and let you be looted by whoever gets there first. I'm erasing you from the list of nations. You'll be totally gone. And you'll get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because Moab was like, 'LOL, Judah is nothing special,' I'm gonna expose Moab's whole side by letting its border towns get attacked—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim. I'm lumping Moab in with Ammon and giving them to the easterners to take over. Ammon will be a nobody. I'm gonna punish Moab hard. And they'll get that I am God.

God, the Master, says: Because Edom was extra petty and went for revenge against Judah, acting all vengeful and out of line, I, God, the Master, am coming for Edom. I'll wipe out everyone, people and animals. I'll waste the whole place—bodies will be stacked from Teman to Dedan. I'll use my own people, Israel, to serve my revenge on Edom. My anger will be their fuel. And they'll know it's my payback. That's a decree from God the Master.

God, the Master, says: Because the Philistines were so spiteful with their revenge—holding onto that grudge for centuries!—and tried their best to destroy Judah, I, God, the Master, am coming for the Philistines. I'll take down the Cretans and anyone else left on the coast. It's gonna be huge acts of revenge, massive punishments! When I finally bring my vengeance, they'll know for sure that I am God."

title: Tyre's Epic Downfall for Hating on Jerusalem
paragraphs: So, in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, God hit me up with a message. He said, "Son of man, Tyre was lowkey celebrating when they heard Jerusalem was crushed.
They were shouting, 'Let's go! The main gateway city is smashed! Now all their trade is gonna come our way. They're in ruins, and we're about to be loaded.'
"Because of that, the Lord GOD has something to say:

"'I'm coming for you, Tyre. I'm gonna send a ton of nations to crash against you, just like the ocean waves crash on the shore. They're gonna tear down your walls and smash your towers. I'll scrape away all your dirt until you're nothing but bare rock. You'll just be a rocky island in the sea, only good for drying fishnets. For real, I've said it.' This is the decree of the Lord GOD. 'You'll be free loot for all the nations! And all your little towns on the mainland will get wrecked. Then they'll finally get that I am the LORD.'

"The Lord GOD says: 'Check this out! From the north, I'm sending King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon—the king of all kings—to deal with you, Tyre. He's rolling up with horses, chariots, and a massive army. He's gonna wipe out your mainland towns and set up a siege. He'll build ramps right up to your walls and his army will be a wall of shields against you! He'll pound your walls with battering rams and shatter your towers with his weapons. The dust from his army of horses will be so thick you can't see. The noise of his warhorses and chariots pouring through your broken walls will be insane. It'll be like an earthquake hitting a city in total shock. Horses will be running wild in your streets. Your people will be killed, and your huge, strong pillars will fall like they're nothing. The invaders will take all your money and valuables. They'll tear down your nice houses and throw all the rubble—stone and wood—into the ocean. And your famous parties? They're over. No more music, no more good times. I'm gonna turn you into a bare rock, a place just for drying fishnets. You will never be rebuilt. I, the LORD, have spoken. This is the decree of the Lord GOD.'
"This is the Lord GOD's message to Tyre: 'The islands are gonna shake when they hear about your epic collapse, the screams of your wounded people, and all the chaos and killing.'

"'All the princes from the coast will get off their thrones, take off their fancy robes, and dress in clothes of pure fear. They'll sit on the ground, totally shook, horrified by what happened to you. Then they'll start singing a funeral song for you:

"'No way! She's sunk! The famous city on the sea is gone, sunk to the bottom. You and your people were a sea power, making everyone who lived near you scared. But now, the islands are shaking from the sound of your fall. The islands in the sea are trembling from the shock of your collapse.'

"The Lord GOD says: 'When I make you a ghost town, a city with no one left, and when I bring the deep ocean waters to cover you, I'm gonna send you down to the pit with those who died a long, long time ago. I'll make you live down there, in those ancient ruins with the dead. You'll never see the world of the living again. I'll bring terrifying things on you, and that's it for you. People will search for you, but you'll be gone forever.' This is the decree of the Lord GOD."

title: The Epic Rise and Fall of the World's Richest City
paragraphs: God's message hit me up, and it was about Tyre. He said, "Son of man, it's time to sing a sad song for Tyre. Tell Tyre, the city that's basically the world's mall, the gateway to the sea for everyone, 'This is what the Lord God has to say:'

'Yo, Tyre, you're always flexing, 'I'm the perfect ship, a total beauty.' You were basically queen of the seas. Your ship was built with the best stuff—planking from Mount Hermon junipers, a mast from a Lebanon cedar. Your oars were made from super strong Bashan oaks. The decks were cypress from Cyprus, with sick ivory inlays. Your sail? Fancy embroidered linen from Egypt that also worked as your flag. And you had these cool purple awnings on deck, also from Cyprus. Your rowers were pros from Sidon and Arvad, and your own experienced sailors were the main crew. The guys who built and fixed your ship were old-timers from Byblos. Basically, every ship and sailor out there wanted to trade with you.

Your army was stacked with soldiers from all over—Paras, Lud, and Put. They were elite troops looking sharp in their uniforms, and they seriously put you on the map. Your city's security guards were hired from Arvad, Helech, and Gammad. They hung their shields all over your walls, which was like the final perfect touch to your city's good looks.
Tarshish was your biggest business partner because you were loaded. They paid for your stuff with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you too, but they were dealing in people—slaves—and bronze for your goods.
Beth-togarmah traded you workhorses, warhorses, and mules for your products.
The people from Rhodes also did business with you. A bunch of faraway islands traded ivory and ebony with you.
Edom traded with you because you had so much stuff. They gave you agate, purple fabrics, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your products.
Judah and Israel were in on it too. They traded top-tier wheat, millet, honey, oil, and balm for your goods.
Damascus, seeing how much stuff you had, did business with you, trading wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
Danites and Greeks from Uzal traded with you, bringing wrought iron, cinnamon, and spices.
Dedan traded saddle blankets with you.
Arabia and all the sheiks from Kedar traded lambs, rams, and goats with you.
Traders from Sheba and Raamah in South Arabia brought you the best spices, precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden from way out east in Assyria and Media traded with you. They brought fancy clothes, colorful textiles, and detailed carpets to your markets.
The huge Tarshish ships were like your personal cargo fleet, handling all your imports and exports. Man, you were doing big business, ruling the trade routes.

But then your sailors, trying to show off, rowed you into a massive storm. A wind from the east just wrecked your ship in the middle of the ocean. Everything went down—all your expensive goods, your sailors and crew, your shipbuilders and soldiers. All of it, sunk to the bottom of the sea. A total shipwreck. The screams of your sailors were heard all the way on the shore. Sailors everywhere jumped ship, and the veteran seamen swam for their lives. They were all crying, a huge, bitter song of grief for you. They put ashes on their faces, shaved their heads, and wore rough clothes, just wailing over their loss. They sang this funeral song: 'Who on the seas was ever like Tyre!'

'When you sailed the seas with your products, you made so many people happy. Your global trade made kings rich. But now, you're smashed to pieces by the waves, sunk to the bottom of the sea. And everything you ever bought or sold went down with you. Everyone on the shore is just staring in horror. Kings' hair is standing on end, their faces pale and shocked. All the traders of the world are just throwing their hands up like, 'No way this could happen!' But oh, it did.'

title: The King with a God Complex Gets a Reality Check
paragraphs: God's message hit me. He said, "Son of man, go tell the leader of Tyre what God, the Master, has to say:

"You've gotten so proud, walking around thinking, 'I'm a god. I'm sitting on God's throne, ruling the ocean.' But you're just a human, not even close to being a god. You're a mortal who's trying way too hard to be a god. You think you're smarter than Daniel, that no puzzle is too tough for you. Your cleverness made you super rich; you've got stacks of gold and silver. You played the game well, made some sick deals, and earned a ton of cash. But all that money has gone straight to your head, making you arrogant.
"So, God, the Master, says this:

"'Because you're acting like you're a god, I'm warning you: I'm sending foreigners to attack you, the most brutal nations around. They're going to pull out their swords and destroy your reputation for being so smart. They'll pop that ego of yours. They'll knock you off your high horse and bury you at sea. Are you going to tell your killers, 'You can't do this! I'm a god'? To them, you're just another guy. They're killing a man, not a god. You'll die like a stray dog, taken out by strangers—because I've said it. This is a decree from God, the Master.'"
God's message came to me again: "Son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre. Tell him this is a message from God, the Master:

"You seriously had it all. You were in Eden, God's garden, dressed in the most amazing clothes, covered in jewels: carnelian, peridot, moonstone, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald, all set in gold. It was all made for you on the day you were created. You were the chosen cherub, an angelic guardian. I put you on God's holy mountain, and you walked among fiery stones. You were perfect from the day you were made... until evil was found in you. All your business deals made you violent, and you sinned. So I threw you off the mountain of God in disgrace. I kicked you out, you guardian angel. No more walking among fiery gems for you. Your beauty made you arrogant. You traded your wisdom for fame. I threw you down to the ground and let other kings watch and gloat over your downfall. With sin after sin, and your corrupt business practices, you trashed your own sacred places. So I started a fire inside and around you, and it burned you to the ground. Now, you're just a pile of ashes for everyone to see. Anyone who knew you is just shocked, like, 'No way this happened! But it did!'"
God's message came to me: "Son of man, go confront Sidon and preach against it. Say, 'This is a message from God, the Master:

"'Look, Sidon, I'm against you. I'm about to show you who I really am.' They'll know I'm God when I come to bring justice and reveal my holiness. I'm going to send a plague, and there will be violence and death in the streets. People will be dying everywhere as war closes in. Then they'll finally get that I'm not playing around, that I am God.
"Israel won't have to deal with its annoying neighbors anymore, the ones who have been like thorns in their side, treating them with contempt. And they, too, will realize that I am God."

God, the Master, says, "When I bring the people of Israel back from all the nations where they've been scattered, and when I show my holiness through them for all the world to see, they will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. They'll live there safely, build houses, and plant vineyards. And while they're living in peace, I'll bring judgment on all their neighbors who treated them so badly. And they will know that I am their God."

title: Pharaoh's Ego Trip Ends in Disaster
paragraphs: So, back in the tenth year, tenth month, on the twelfth day, God's message hit me up. He said, "Son of man, go confront Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. You need to call him and all of Egypt out. Tell them, this is what the Master GOD says:

'Yo, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, watch yourself. I'm so not on your side. You're like this big, lazy dragon just lounging in the Nile, all like, ‘This is my river. I made it. It’s all mine.’ Well, I'm about to put hooks in your jaw and make all the fish of the Nile cling to your scales. I'm gonna pull you right out of the river, with all those fish still stuck to you. Then I'm gonna drag you out into the desert, you and every last fish. You'll just lie there out in the open, becoming food for wild animals and birds. Then every single person in Egypt will finally get that I am GOD.

'You've been a totally useless support for Israel. When they tried to lean on you, you just splintered and hurt them, and when they put their weight on you, you broke and made them fall flat. So, because of that—this is a message from the Master GOD—I'm bringing a war against you. I'm gonna get rid of your people and your animals, and I'll turn your whole country into a barren wasteland. That's how they'll know that I am GOD.

'Since you were all like, ‘The Nile is mine. I made it. It belongs to me,’ I'm now against you and your rivers. I'm going to turn Egypt into a totally empty, desolate desert, all the way from Migdol down to Syene at the Ethiopian border. You won't see a single person or even an animal. It'll be a ghost town for forty years straight.

'I'm gonna make Egypt the most desolate place ever. For forty years, its cities will be the most ruined of all ruined cities. I'll scatter the Egyptians all over the world, sending them into exile in every direction.

'But,' says the Master GOD, 'that's not the end of the story. After those forty years are up, I'll gather the Egyptians back from all the places they were scattered. I'll restore Egypt and bring them back to Pathros, where they first started. They'll have to start over from the very beginning. They'll be at the very bottom of all the nations, and they'll stay there. They're never climbing back up to be a world power again. Israel will never be tempted to depend on Egypt again. Egypt will just be a reminder of their past mistakes. Then they will know that I am the Master GOD.'

Then, in the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, God's message came to me again: "Son of man, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon totally wore out his army fighting against Tyre. They worked themselves to the bone and got nothing out of it.

"So, the Master GOD says, 'I'm giving Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He's going to take all its wealth and loot the place clean. That'll be the payment for his army. He was working for me all that time and didn't get paid. So, Egypt is his paycheck. That's a decree from the Master GOD.
"'And when that happens, I'll give fresh hope to Israel—a new dawn is coming!—and I'll give you, Ezekiel, the confidence to speak boldly. And they will finally realize that I am GOD.'"

title: Egypt's Epic Fail & Broken Arms
paragraphs: God, the boss, hit me up: "Yo, son of man, preach this. Give 'em the message from God, the Master. And just wail:

"'It's doomsday!' Time is totally up. God's huge day of judgment is right around the corner. Thick clouds are rolling in. It's the end for the nations. Death is gonna pour down on Egypt. Ethiopia will be paralyzed with terror when they see the Egyptians getting wrecked, their stuff hauled off, and their whole foundation demolished. And Ethiopia, Put, Lud, Arabia, Libya—all of Egypt’s old crew—are gonna go down right along with them.
"'God says:

"'Egypt’s squad will fall and their proud strength will totally collapse—from Migdol up north to Syene down south, it's gonna be a massive slaughter in Egypt. That's a decree from God, the Master. Egypt, the most wrecked of the wrecked, its cities wasted beyond belief, will finally get that I am God when I burn it down and all its helpers get knocked out flat.
"'When that goes down, I’ll send messengers by ship to sound the alarm for the super chill Ethiopians. They’ll be totally freaked out. Egypt is doomed! Judgment is coming.
"'God, the Master, says:

"'I’m gonna put a stop to Egypt’s flexing. And I'll use King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to do it. He and his army, the most savage crew out there, will be sent to destroy the country. They’ll pull out their swords and fill Egypt with bodies. I’ll dry up the Nile River and sell off the land to a bunch of crooks. I’ll hire some outsiders to come in and just waste the country, strip it clean. I, God, have spoken.
"'And now this is what God, the Master, says:

"'I’m gonna smash all the fake gods; I’ll knock over all those giant statues in Memphis. The prince of Egypt will be gone for good, and in his place, I’ll just put fear—fear all over Egypt! I’ll demolish Pathros, burn Zoan to the ground, and punish Thebes. I'll pour my anger on Pelusium, Egypt’s main fort, and knock Thebes off its proud pedestal. I’ll set Egypt on fire: Pelusium will be writhing in pain, Thebes will get blown away, and Memphis will be violated. The young soldiers of On and Pi-beseth will be killed and the cities will be exiled. It's gonna be a dark day for Tahpanhes when I shatter Egypt, when I break its power and end its arrogant oppression. She’ll disappear in a cloud of dust, and her cities will be hauled off as exiles. That’s how I’ll punish Egypt, and that’s how she’ll finally get that I am God.'"
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, God's message came to me:
"Son of man, I’ve broken the arm of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. And look! It hasn't been fixed. No cast has been put on it so the bones can heal, so he can even use a sword again.

"So, God, the Master, says, I am so done with Pharaoh king of Egypt and I'm gonna go ahead and break his other arm—both arms broken! There’s no way he’ll ever swing a sword again. I’ll scatter the Egyptians all over the world. I’ll make the arms of the king of Babylon strong and put my sword in his hand, but I’ll break Pharaoh's arms and he’ll just groan like someone who's been fatally wounded. I’ll make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh's arms will just go limp. The Egyptians will finally get that I am God when I put my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon. He’ll use it against Egypt and I’ll scatter the Egyptians all over the world. Then they’ll know for real that I am God."

title: The Epic Fall of the World's Biggest Tree
paragraphs: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, God's message hit me. He said, "Son of man, go tell Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, arrogant as he is:

"'Who do you, sitting on top of the world, even think you are? Just look at Assyria. It was like a massive tree, a giant Lebanon cedar with gorgeous branches making cool shade. It was skyscraper-high, literally piercing the clouds. It was so well-watered, like it was plugged into the deep springs of the earth, with rivers flowing all around it and feeding all the other trees in the forest. It was huge, making all the other trees look tiny. Its branches were thick, its limbs were long, and its roots went deep into the earth's water supply. All the birds nested in its branches. All the wild animals had their babies under it. The most powerful nations lived in its shade. It was breathtakingly majestic—the sheer reach of its branches and the depth of its roots! Not a single cedar in God's own garden could compare. No pine tree was even close. The mightiest oaks looked like little bushes next to it. Seriously, no tree in God's garden was in the same league of beauty. I made it beautiful, a masterpiece of branches and leaves, and it was the envy of every single tree in Eden, God's garden.'

"Therefore, God, the Master, says, 'Because it shot up like a skyscraper, piercing the clouds, and got all cocky and proud of its height, I handed it over to a world-famous leader to hold it accountable for its evil. I was done with it. Foreigners, a seriously brutal bunch, came and chopped it down on the mountains. Its branches were scattered through all the valleys, and its broken limbs clogged up all the streams and rivers. Once its shade was gone, everyone just left. It wasn't a tree anymore—just a log. Now, birds just perch on the dead log, and wild animals dig burrows under it.'

"'That's the end of the 'big tree' nations. No more trees fed by the deep springs, no more cloud-piercing trees, no more earthly trees trying to take over. They're all destined for death—back to the dirt, just like all humans, because it's 'dust to dust' for everyone.'

"'This is the message from God, the Master: On the day the Big Tree had its funeral, I made the deep springs mourn. I stopped the rivers from flowing, held back the great seas, and made the Lebanon mountains wear black. All the trees of the forest fainted and collapsed. I made the whole world shake when it crashed, and I threw it down into the underworld to be with everything else that gets buried. All the trees of Eden, even the finest and best trees of Lebanon that were so well-watered, were actually relieved—they had gone down to the underworld with it—along with everyone who had lived in its shade and all who had been killed.'

"'So, which of the trees of Eden could even come close to you in splendor and size? But guess what? You're also destined to be chopped down and join the trees of Eden in the underworld, to be just another dead log stacked with all the other dead logs, among the uncircumcised who are dead and buried.'
"'This is about Pharaoh, arrogant as he is.'
"'A decree from God, the Master.'"

title: Pharaoh's Diss Track: Welcome to the Underworld
paragraphs: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, God’s message hit me up. He said, “Son of man, it’s time to drop a funeral track for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Tell him this:
‘You really think you’re some big-shot lion, prowling around the world stage. Bro, you’re more like a sea monster thrashing around in the ocean, making a mess.
This is what the Lord GOD is saying:

‘I’m about to cast my net on you—and a whole squad of nations is gonna help me out—and I’ll drag you out with it. I’ll just dump you on the ground, right out in the open. Then I’m inviting all the vultures and crows for a massive feast on your dead body. I’ll even get wild animals from all over to come and get a piece. I’m gonna scatter your body parts all over the mountains and fill the valleys with your bones. The whole country, all the way to the mountains, will be soaked in your blood. It’s gonna fill up every single ditch. When I take you out, I’m shutting down the sky. The stars will go dark, I’ll block the sun with a cloud, and the moon will be switched off. I’ll turn off every light in the sky above you and throw your whole country into darkness. That’s a promise from the Lord GOD. I’m gonna shake up the whole world when I drag you off as a prisoner to countries you’ve never even heard of. People will be shook when they see what I’ve done to you. Kings will literally tremble when they see it. I’ll wave my sword, and they’ll be shaking in their boots. The day you fall, they’ll all be terrified, thinking, ‘That could’ve been me!’
This is what the Lord GOD is saying:

‘The king of Babylon’s sword is coming for you. I’m gonna use the swords of the best fighters, the most brutal nations out there, to crush your pride. They’re gonna totally wreck Egypt’s arrogance and pop that inflated ego. I’ll destroy all the cattle that graze by the river. No person or animal will ever make those waters muddy again. I’ll make their springs and streams run clear, super smooth. That’s a promise from the Lord GOD. When I turn Egypt into a wasteland and strip it of everything it has, when I strike down everyone who lives there, then they’ll finally get that I am GOD.’
This is a funeral song. So sing it. Let the young women of the nations sing it. Sing it for Egypt and for the end of all its hype.” A decree from the Lord GOD.
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the first month, God’s message came to me:

“Son of man, cry over Egypt’s flexing. Send her down. Send Egypt and her proud allies to the underworld, down to the land of the dead. Tell them, ‘You think you’re all that? Get down here and join the rest of the pagans in this cursed grave!’

“She’s gonna be thrown in with everyone who died in battle. The sword is ready. Drag her and all her hype away! All the big shots and their crews down in the grave will greet them like, ‘Welcome to the pagan graveyard! Come join the rest of the war victims!’

“Assyria is there with its whole crew, the entire nation is a cemetery. Their graves are in the deepest part of the pit, a whole field of graves, all of them killed in battle—these were the same people who used to terrorize the living.

“Elam is there with all its pride, a whole cemetery of them—all killed in battle, thrown into a pagan grave with the rest of the dead, these guys who used to terrorize the living. Now they have to carry their shame with everyone else in the pit. They made a whole section for the proud dead, decorated with pagan graves, all slaughtered in battle. They used to be terrifying, but now they carry their shame down with the others into the deep. They’re in the section for the battle-slain.

“Meshech-tubal is there with all its pride, a cemetery in unholy ground, thrown in with those slaughtered in battle—which is what they get for terrorizing the living. Now they carry their shame down with the others into the deep. They’re in the section for the slain. They’re kept separate from the legendary heroes, the ancient giants who were buried in full armor, with their swords under their heads and shields on their bones, the same heroes who once spread terror everywhere.
“And you, Egypt, you’ll be thrown into a pagan grave, right along with all the others, in the section for the slain.
“Edom is there, with its kings and princes. Even though they were super powerful, they’re now thrown into a pagan grave with everyone else headed for the pit.

“The princes of the north are there, every single one of them, and all the Sidonians who now carry their shame to their graves—all that terror they spread with their power is gone!—dumped in an unholy grave with those killed in battle, carrying their shame with the others headed for the deep.
“Pharaoh will see them all and, arrogant as he is, will actually feel better seeing all the company he has—Pharaoh and his whole slaughtered army. A decree from the Lord GOD.
“I used him to spread terror in the land of the living, and now I’m dumping him in a pagan grave with those killed by the sword—Pharaoh and all his hype. A decree from the Lord GOD.”

title: The Watchman's Job is Lowkey a Big Deal
paragraphs: God hit me up and said, "Yo, son of man, tell your people, 'If I send an army to attack this land, and the people choose one of their own to be a watchman, and if that watchman sees the army coming and blows the trumpet to warn everyone, then if someone hears the trumpet but ignores it and the army comes and gets them, that's on them. They heard the warning but didn't listen—it's their own fault. If they had paid attention, they would've saved their own life.

'But if the watchman sees the army coming and doesn't blow the trumpet to warn the people, and the army comes and takes someone, I'm gonna hold the watchman responsible for that person's death because they weren't warned.'

"You, son of man, are that watchman. I've made you a watchman for Israel. As soon as you hear a message from me, you have to warn them. If I tell a wicked person, 'You're on a fast track to death!' and you don't say anything to warn them to change their ways, they'll die in their sins without being warned, and I'll hold you responsible for their death. But if you do warn them to change their ways and they don't, they'll die in their sins, but at least you'll have saved yourself.
"Son of man, go talk to Israel. Tell them, 'You've been saying, “Our mistakes and sins are crushing us. We're just wasting away. How are we supposed to keep living?”'

"Tell them, 'As surely as I am the living God, I don't get any joy from the death of the wicked. I want the wicked to turn from their ways and live. Turn your life around! Stop doing evil! Why would you choose to die, Israel?'

"And there's more, son of man. Tell your people, 'A good person's good life won't save them if they decide to rebel, and a bad person's bad life won't stop them from turning their life around. A good person who sins can't just expect to live because they were good before. It's true that I tell good people, “Live! Be alive!” But if they start trusting in their own good deeds and turn to evil, all that good they did won't mean anything. They'll die for the evil they've done.

"'On the other hand, if I tell a wicked person, “You're going to die for your wicked life,” and they turn away from their sin and start living a righteous and just life—like being generous to those who are struggling, giving back what they stole, and living in a way that helps others—they will live. They won't die. None of their past sins will be held against them. They're doing what's right and living a good life. They will live.

"'Your people are saying, “God's way isn't fair.” But it's their way of living that's not fair. When good people stop living good lives and start sinning, they'll die for it. And when a wicked person turns away from their wicked life and starts living a just and righteous life, they'll come alive.
"'And you all still keep saying, “God's way isn't fair.” We'll see about that, Israel. I'm going to judge every single one of you based on how you live.'"
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a survivor from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen."
The evening before that survivor showed up, God's hand was on me and He gave me my voice back. By the time the guy arrived in the morning, I was able to speak. I could talk again.

God's message came to me: "Son of man, the people who are living in the ruins back in Israel are saying, 'Abraham was just one guy and he owned this whole country. But there are a lot of us. So for sure, this land belongs to us.'

"So tell them, 'God the Master says, You eat meat with blood in it, you worship fake idols, you murder people whenever you want—and you really think you're going to own this land? You rely on your weapons, you do disgusting things, you sleep with whoever, whenever. And you still think you're going to own this land?'

"Tell them this, Ezekiel: 'This is a message from God, the Master. As surely as I am the living God, those who are still alive in the ruins will be killed. Anyone out in the open, I'll feed to wild animals. Anyone hiding in mountain fortresses and caves will die of disease. I'll turn this country into a total wasteland—no more arrogant bullies! The mountains of Israel will become so empty and dangerous that no one will even dare to go through them.'
"They'll know that I am God when I destroy the country because of all the disgusting things they've done.

"As for you, son of man, you've become the talk of the town. Your people gather on street corners and in front of their houses and say, 'Let's go hear the latest message from God.' They all show up and sit with you. They listen to what you say, but they don't actually do any of it. They'll say nice things to you, but all they really care about is making money and getting ahead. To them, you're just entertainment—like a singer with a sad love song and a guitar. They love to hear you talk, but it doesn't change anything.
"But when all this stuff actually happens—and trust me, it's going to happen!—then they'll realize that a real prophet was among them."

title: God Fires the Shady Leaders & Becomes the GOAT Shepherd
paragraphs: God's message hit me. He said, "Yo, son of man, call out the so-called shepherds of Israel. Yeah, you heard me. Tell those leaders, 'The big boss, God, is saying: It's over for you shepherds of Israel who are only looking out for number one. Aren't shepherds supposed to, like, feed the sheep? You're drinking the milk, making clothes from the wool, and having lamb chops for dinner, but you're not actually feeding the sheep. You don't help the weak ones get stronger, you don't take care of the sick, you don't patch up the injured, you don't go after the ones who've wandered off, and you don't look for the lost. You just bully them and boss them around. And now they're scattered all over the place because there was no real shepherd—scattered and basically a free-for-all for wolves and coyotes. My sheep are scattered, totally exposed and vulnerable on every mountain and hill. My flock is spread across the whole world, and not a single person is out there looking for them!'

'So, listen up, you shepherds, this is God's message: As sure as I'm the living God—this is a decree from the Master, God—because my sheep were turned into easy prey, basically a buffet for wolves because you shepherds just ignored them and fed yourselves, you better listen to what God has to say now.'

'Watch out! I'm coming for you shepherds, and I'm taking my sheep back. You're fired from being shepherds of my flock. No more leaders who just feed themselves! I'm rescuing my sheep from your greed. You're not going to be using my sheep for your own gain anymore!'

'God, the Master, says: From now on, I'm taking over as the shepherd myself. I'm going to go look for them. Just like a shepherd goes after their flock when it gets scattered, I'm going after my sheep. I'll rescue them from all the places they were scattered to during the dark times. I'll bring them back from other nations, gather them from foreign countries, and bring them back to their own land. I'll feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams, right where they belong. I'll lead them to amazing pastures so they can chill on the mountain pastures of Israel, graze peacefully, and eat from the best pastures on the mountains of Israel. And I, myself, will be the shepherd of my sheep. I'll make sure they get all the rest they need. I'll go after the lost ones, bring back the strays, patch up the injured, build up the weak, and I'll keep an eye on the strong ones so they don't get taken advantage of.'

'And as for you, my precious flock, I'm stepping in to judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats. Aren't you happy just eating in a good pasture without trying to claim the whole thing? Can't you just drink from the clean stream without making it all muddy with your feet? Why do the rest of my sheep have to deal with trampled grass and dirty water?'

'Because of this, God, the Master, says: I'm personally stepping in to make things right between the fat sheep and the skinny sheep. Because you pushed your way through with your shoulder and your backside and used your horns to butt all the weaker animals until you scattered them everywhere, I'm going to come and save my precious flock. They won't be pushed around anymore. I'll step in and sort things out between all the sheep.'

'I'm going to set up one shepherd to rule them all: my servant David. He will feed them. He will be their true shepherd. And I, God, will be their God. My servant David will be their leader. I, God, have said it.'

'I'll make a peace treaty with them. I'll get rid of all the dangerous animals from the country so the sheep can live safely in the wild and even sleep in the forest. I'll make them and everything around my hill a huge blessing. I'll send down tons of rain when it's needed—literal showers of blessing! The trees will be full of fruit, the ground will produce amazing crops, they'll feel safe and secure in their own land, and they'll know for sure that I am God when I break them free from their slavery and rescue them from their slave masters.'

'They won't be taken advantage of by other nations or attacked by wild animals anymore. They'll live in safety and peace, with nothing to fear. I'll give them lush gardens, overflowing with vegetables—no more starving, no more being made fun of by outsiders.'
'They'll know, without a doubt, that I, God, am their God, that I'm with them, and that they, the people of Israel, are my people. This is a decree from God, the Master.'
'You are my precious flock, the flock of my pasture, my human flock. And I am your God. A decree from God, the Master.'

title: God's Clapback on Mount Seir
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up: “Yo, son of man, go call out Mount Seir. Drop this prophecy on them! Tell them, ‘God, the Boss, is saying this:

“‘I’m about to come for you, Mount Seir. I’m stepping in and turning you into a total wreck. I’ll make your towns just piles of rocks. There’ll be nothing left of you. Then you’ll know for real that I am God.

“‘I’m doing this ‘cause you’ve held on to this ancient beef with Israel. You went after them so hard when they were already at their lowest, facing their final consequence. So, for real, as the living God, I’m setting you up for a massive L. Since you were so about that violent life, you’re gonna get chased by it. I’ll turn Mount Seir into a wasteland. Nobody’s gonna be coming or going. I’ll cover your mountains with bodies. Dead bodies everywhere—on your hills, in your valleys, in your ditches. I’ll leave you in ruins, and your towns will be ghost towns—literally zero population. Then you’ll get it that I am God.

“‘And because you were like, “These two nations, these two countries? They’re mine. I’m taking over” (even though God was right there, watching and listening), I’m gonna flip all that hate and anger you have right back at you. You’ll know I’m not playing when I bring my judgment down on you. Then you’ll finally realize that I, God, heard all the trash you talked about the mountains of Israel, saying, “They’re toast, and we’re gonna feast.” You’ve been acting all tough, talking big, disrespectfully challenging me. And trust me, I’ve heard every word.

“‘So here’s the final word from God, the Master: The whole world is gonna cheer when I take you down. Since you were out there celebrating, thinking it was so great when Israel lost everything, I’m gonna do the same to you: total destruction. Mount Seir is gonna be destroyed—yeah, every single bit of Edom. Then they’ll finally get that I am God!’”

title: Israel's Epic Comeback Story
paragraphs: “Alright, son of man, it's time to speak to the mountains of Israel. Tell them, ‘Hey, mountains of Israel, listen to God’s message. The big boss, God, is saying this: Your enemies were bragging, like, ‘Awesome! Those ancient hills are ours now!’ So, here’s what God, the Master, has to say about it: Because all these nations ganged up on you, tearing you apart, taking pieces of you for themselves, and you became the punchline of everyone's jokes, you need to listen up. This is God’s message to the mountains, hills, valleys, and all the trashed, empty towns that got looted and laughed at by the nations around you. God, the Master, says: I am seriously fired up and angry at those other nations, especially Edom. They straight-up stole my land with total disrespect and violence, just grabbing it for themselves.’

“So go ahead, preach to the land of Israel, to its mountains, hills, and valleys. Tell them: ‘This is a message from God, the Master: Look, I'm angry, and I care about you. I'm speaking up because you've been totally humiliated by the other nations. So I, God, the Master, swear to you that it's their turn now. Those nations around you are about to get humiliated themselves.

“‘But you, mountains of Israel, you’re about to have a major glow-up. You'll grow new branches and produce fruit for my people, Israel, because they're coming home soon! See? I'm on your side again. You'll be farmed and planted just like before. I'll make sure your population booms all over Israel. The towns will be full of people again, and the ruins will be rebuilt. I'll fill this land with life—people and animals. The whole country will be bursting with life, more than ever before, with your towns as full as they were in the good old days. I'm going to treat you even better than I ever have. And then you'll know for sure that I am God. I'll bring my own people, Israel, to take care of you, and you will be their special inheritance. You'll never be a harsh land that causes them pain again.

“‘God, the Master, says: You've got this reputation for being a land that 'eats' its own people and causes families to fail. Well, I'm telling you now, that's over. You won't be known for that anymore. That's a promise from God, the Master. I won't let other nations mock you or look down on you ever again. You won't be a land that brings failure. That's a promise from God, the Master.’”

God’s message came to me again: “Son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own land, they totally trashed it with their lifestyle. I was furious with them because of the violence and corruption they spread everywhere. They were polluting the country with their murders and their fake gods, so I got fed up. I kicked them out and scattered them among other nations, judging them for how they lived. But wherever they went, they gave me a bad name. People would say, ‘These are supposedly God’s people, but they got kicked out of his land.’ It really hurt my holy reputation, which the people of Israel dragged through the mud in every country they went to.

“So, tell the house of Israel, ‘This is a message from God, the Master: I’m not doing this for your sake, Israel. I’m doing it for MY sake, to restore my holy name that you’ve ruined all over the world. I’m about to show everyone how great and holy my name is—the name you’ve dishonored everywhere. Then, all the nations will realize that I am God. They'll see my holiness on display through you, right before their eyes.

“‘Here’s the plan: I’m going to grab you from all those countries, gather you up, and bring you back to your own land. I’ll wash you clean with pure water. I’m going to give you a new heart and a new spirit. I’ll take out that hard, stubborn heart of stone and replace it with a heart that truly wants to follow me. I’ll put my Spirit inside you, empowering you to live by my rules and follow my commands. You’ll live in the land I promised your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God!

“‘I’ll save you from all the nasty stuff you've been into. I’ll command the fields to produce massive harvests, so you’ll never have to deal with famine again. I’ll make your trees and crops flourish. No other nation will be able to diss you for being hungry ever again.
“‘And then you’ll look back on your messed-up past—all the evil and shameful things you did—and you’ll be completely disgusted with yourselves. You'll finally get how messed up your actions were.
“‘But get this straight—I’m not doing this for you. Seriously. You should be ashamed of the huge mess you made of everything, Israel!

“‘This is a message from God, the Master: On the day I finally clean you up from all your filth, I’ll also make your cities livable again. The ruins will be rebuilt. The abandoned land will be cultivated, no longer just a field of weeds that everyone ignores. People will be shocked and say, ‘Wow, this wasteland has turned into a Garden of Eden! And all those ruined, destroyed cities are now packed with people and thriving!’ The nations still around you will know that I, God, am the one who rebuilds ruins and replants wastelands. I, God, have said it, and I will do it.

“‘And here’s another thing from God, the Master: I’m going to do what Israel asks for once again. I’ll make their population explode like a flock of sheep. The ruined cities will be as crowded with people as Jerusalem is with sheep during the big festivals. And then they will know that I am God.’”

title: The Ultimate Glow-Up: Bone Edition
paragraphs: God just grabbed me. His Spirit yoinked me and dropped me in this huge open field that was literally just covered in bones. He had me walk all around them—so many bones! They were scattered everywhere, super dry and bleached out by the sun.
He asked me, “Yo, son of man, can these bones actually live?”
I was like, “Master God, for real, only you know the answer to that.”
He told me, “Prophesy to these bones. Be like, ‘Yo, dry bones, listen up to God’s message!’”

Then God, the Master, said to the dry bones, “Watch this. I’m about to give you life, and you’re gonna be alive again. I’ll hook you up with muscles, put some meat back on you, cover you with skin, and breathe life into you. You’ll be alive, and you’ll know for sure that I am God!”

So I did what he said. As I was prophesying, there was this crazy sound, like a huge rustling noise! The bones started moving and connecting, bone to bone. I just kept watching. Muscles started forming, then flesh grew on the bones, and then skin covered it all. But, plot twist, they still weren’t breathing.
He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man. Tell the breath, ‘God, the Master, says, Come from all over. Come, breath. Breathe on these dead bodies. Bring them to life!’”
So I prophesied, just like he told me to. The breath went into them, and they came back to life! They all stood up on their feet, a massive army.
Then God told me, “Son of man, these bones? They represent the entire nation of Israel. Listen to what they’re saying: ‘Our bones are all dried up, we’ve lost all hope, we’re totally done for.’

“So, prophesy to them. Tell them, ‘God, the Master, says: I’m gonna open up your graves and bring you out alive—my people! Then I’ll take you straight back to the land of Israel. When I open your graves and bring you out, you’ll finally get that I am God. I’ll breathe my own life into you, and you’ll live. Then I’ll lead you right back to your own land, and you’ll know that I am God. I said it, and I’m gonna do it. That’s a promise from God.’”

God’s message came to me again: “You, son of man, grab a stick and write on it, ‘For Judah and his Israelite crew.’ Then get another stick and write on it, ‘For Joseph—Ephraim’s stick, with all his Israelite crew.’ Then, tie the two sticks together so you’re holding just one stick.

“When your people ask you, ‘Uh, you gonna tell us what you’re doing?’ tell them, ‘God, the Master, says, Watch me! I’m gonna take the Joseph stick that’s in Ephraim’s hand, with all the tribes connected to him, and I’ll put the Judah stick on it. I’ll make them into one single stick. I’m holding one stick.’

“Then hold up the sticks you wrote on so everyone can see them. Tell them, ‘God, the Master, says, Watch me! I’m pulling the Israelites out of all the countries where they were exiled. I’ll gather them from everywhere and bring them back home. I’ll make them one nation in their own land, on the mountains of Israel, and they’ll have one king—one king for all of them. They’ll never be split into two nations or two kingdoms again. They won’t mess up their lives with fake gods, gross idols, and all that rebellious stuff anymore. I’ll save them from all their old sinful habits. I’ll clean them up. They’ll be my people! And I’ll be their God! My boy David will be their king, and they’ll all follow one leader.

“‘They’ll follow my rules and stick to my commands. They’ll live in the same land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where their ancestors lived. They and their kids and their grandkids will live there forever, and my servant David will be their leader forever. I’ll make a peace treaty with them that will last forever, an unbreakable promise. I’ll make them feel safe and I’ll put my holy temple right in the middle of their lives, forever. I’ll live right there with them. I’ll be their God! They’ll be my people!
“‘All the other nations will know that I, God, have made Israel holy when my temple is set up right in the center of their lives, forever.’”

title: God vs. Gog: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: God’s message hit me up. He said, “Yo, son of man, you need to go confront Gog, this dude from the land of Magog who’s the head honcho of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him. Tell him, ‘The Master God says: Watch yourself, Gog. I’m totally against you, leader of Meshech and Tubal. I’m gonna spin you around, put hooks in your jaws, and drag you and your whole army out—all your horses and riders decked out in armor, with all their shields and swords, a massive crew ready to fight. Persia, Cush, and Put will be with them, also armed to the teeth, plus Gomer and its army, and Beth-togarmah from way up north with its crew. Yeah, a ton of nations are rolling with you.’

‘Get ready for a fight, you and this whole squad you’ve assembled. You’re in charge, so just wait for my signal. After a long time, you’ll get your orders. Way down the line, you’ll show up in a country that’s just recovered from a crazy war. People from all over will be gathered on the mountains of Israel, which were a wasteland for ages. These people were brought back from all over and are now living all safe and sound. You’ll roll in like a thunderstorm, like a massive cloud covering the whole land, you and all your troops.’

‘A message from the Master God: At that time, you’ll start scheming and come up with a seriously evil plan. You’ll be like, “I’m gonna invade this country that has zero defenses. I’ll attack these people who are just chilling, living their lives without a care, no gates on their cities, no locks on their doors. I’m gonna go in and just plunder the whole place, clean them out completely. This country is rebuilt from nothing, full of people who came back from exile, and their economy is booming right in the center of everything.”’

‘Sheba and Dedan and Tarshish, all these traders just trying to make a quick buck, will be like, “Whoa, so you’re just here to wreck the place and get rich, huh? You brought your whole army just to cash out?”’

“So, son of man, prophesy! Tell Gog, ‘This is a message from the Master God: When my people Israel are living securely, are you really gonna make a move? You’ll come down from the far north, you and your massive mob of armies, charging in on your horses like a tidal wave, and you’ll invade my people Israel, covering the land like a giant cloud. When the time is right, I’m gonna unleash you on my land. Why? So that all the nations will finally get who I am. They’ll see me put my holiness on full display right through you, Gog, for everyone to see.’

‘A message from the Master God: Remember years ago when I spoke through my servants, the prophets of Israel? Weren’t you the one I was talking about? Year after year, they prophesied that I would bring you against them. And when that day comes, Gog, when you attack the land of Israel—this is a decree from the Master God—my anger is going to explode. Fueled by my burning jealousy, I’m telling you, there will be a massive earthquake that will rock the land of Israel. The fish, the birds, the wild animals—even the tiniest bugs!—and every single person will tremble before me. Mountains will literally fall apart, and cliffs will crumble. I’ll call for an all-out war against you, Gog—a decree from the Master God—and your own guys will start fighting each other on the mountains of Israel. I’ll hit you with everything I’ve got: plagues, massacres, insane rain and hailstorms, and even volcanic lava pouring down on you and all your troops and the people with you.’
‘I’m going to show you just how great and holy I am. I’ll make myself known to the whole world. Then you’ll finally realize that I am God.’”

title: God's Ultimate Takedown: Gog Gets Wrecked
paragraphs: “Alright, go prophesy against Gog. Tell him, ‘This is a message from the one and only God, the Master: I’m so against you, Gog, you leader of Meshech and Tubal. I’m about to turn you around, drag you all the way from the far north, and bring you down hard on the mountains of Israel. Then I’ll smack that bow right out of your left hand and the arrows from your right. You and your whole crew, and everyone with you, are gonna get taken out on the mountains of Israel. I’m gonna serve you up as a feast for all the scavenger birds and wild animals. You’ll fall in the middle of an open field. I’ve said it, and it’s gonna happen. That’s a decree from God, the Master.’
“I’m gonna set fire to Magog and all those islands way out there where people think they’re so safe. And then they’ll finally get it that I am God.
“I’m going to make my holy name known among my people, Israel. I’m never again gonna let my name get disrespected. Then all the other nations will realize that I, God, am the Holy One in Israel.
“It’s coming! For real, it’s going to happen! This is the day I’ve been talking about.

“The people from the cities of Israel will come out and build a huge bonfire with all the enemy’s weapons. They’ll be throwing on shields, big and small, bows and arrows, clubs and spears. This fire will burn for seven whole years. They won’t even need to chop wood from the forest; they’ll have plenty of weapons to fuel the fire. They’re gonna take back what was taken from them and rob the ones who robbed them. That’s a decree from God, the Master.

“When that time comes, I’ll give Gog a burial plot right in Israel, in the Valley of the Travelers, just east of the sea. It’s gonna be so massive it’ll block the road for anyone trying to pass through. That’s where they’ll bury Gog and his entire army. They’ll even name the place ‘The Valley of Gog’s Horde.’

“The people of Israel will spend seven months burying all the bodies to clean up the land. Everyone will pitch in. It’ll be a huge day for them, and I’ll get the glory for it. They’ll hire a full-time crew just to handle the cleanup, going through the country looking for any leftover bodies. After seven months, they’ll do one last major search. If anyone spots a bone, they’ll put up a marker so the burial crew can come get it and bury it in the mass grave, ‘The Valley of Gog’s Horde.’ (There’s even a town nearby that will be called ‘Horde-ville’ or Hamonah.) That’s how they’ll get the land all cleaned up.

“Alright, God, the Master, says this: Call all the birds! Call all the wild animals! Tell them, ‘Get over here! Gather around for this crazy sacrificial meal I’m cooking up for you on the mountains of Israel. You’re gonna eat meat and drink blood. You’ll be feasting on the bodies of absolute legends and drinking the blood of world-famous princes like they were a bunch of rams, lambs, goats, and bulls—the best of the best. At this sacrificial meal I’m making, you’ll eat fat until you’re stuffed and drink blood until you’re wasted. You’ll chow down on horses and their riders, heroes and all kinds of warriors at the table I’m setting for you.’ That’s a decree from God, the Master.

“I’m gonna show off my glory to all the nations, and they’ll all see my judgment in action. From that day forward, Israel will know for sure that I am their God. And the other nations will finally understand that Israel was sent into exile because of their own sins. They were unfaithful to me, so I turned my back on them. I let their enemies take them down, and they were all killed. I gave them what they deserved for their messed-up, sinful lives. I turned away and wouldn’t even look at them.

“But now, I’m bringing Jacob back from exile. I’m going to have compassion on all the people of Israel, and I’ll be super protective of my holy name. The memory of their shame and all the times they betrayed me will eventually fade away, especially when they’re living securely in their own land, totally safe and without fear. Once I’ve brought them back from other countries and gathered them from enemy lands, I’ll use them to show how holy I am for all the nations to see. Then they’ll know that I am their God. Because even though I sent them away into exile, I’m gonna gather them all back to their own land, not leaving a single person behind. After I pour my Spirit on Israel and fill them with my life, I’ll never turn away from them again. I’ll look them right in the face. That’s a decree from God, the Master.”

title: God's Epic Temple Blueprint Reveal
paragraphs: So, in the 25th year of our exile, right at the start of the year, on the 10th day of the month—which was 14 years after Jerusalem got wrecked—God’s hand came on me and boom, I was there. He took me in this wild vision to Israel and dropped me on a super high mountain. Down south, there were these buildings that looked like a whole city. He took me over, and I met this guy who was shining like bronze. He was standing at the gate holding a linen rope and a measuring stick.

The guy said to me, “Yo, son of man, you gotta watch this and listen up. Pay real close attention to everything I’m about to show you. This is why you’re here. Then you gotta go tell Israel everything you see.”

First thing I saw was this massive wall all around the Temple area. The measuring stick the guy had was about 10 feet long. He measured the wall's thickness: a solid 10 feet. The height was 10 feet too.

He walked into the east-facing gate and went up the seven steps. He measured the entrance of the gate: 10 feet deep. On both sides of the hallway, there were these little rooms, each one a 10-foot cube, with 7.5-foot thick walls between them. The inner doorway that led to the porch facing the Temple courtyard was also 10 feet deep.
Then he measured the porch of the gate: 12 feet deep, with pillars on the sides that were 3 feet thick. This porch opened up right into the Temple courtyard.
Inside this east gate, there were three of those little rooms on each side. Each room was the same size and the walls between them were identical.
He measured the outside entrance to the gate: 15 feet wide and 19.5 feet deep.
In front of each little room was a low wall, about 18 inches high. The rooms themselves were 10-foot squares.
He measured the width of the whole gate area from the roof's edge on one side to the other: 37.5 feet from top edge to top edge.
He measured the inside walls of the gate area: 90 feet to the porch that led into the courtyard.
The distance from the gate entrance to the far end of the porch was 75 feet.

The little rooms and their walls inside the gate had narrow windows all around. The porch did too. All the windows faced inward. The doorframes between the rooms had palm trees carved on them, which is pretty cool.

The man then led me to the outer courtyard and all its rooms. There was a paved walkway connecting the courtyard gates. Thirty rooms were lined up along the courtyard. The walkway was the same length as the gateways, running alongside them. This was the walkway for the outer courtyard. He measured the distance from the front of the entrance gate across to the entrance of the inner court: 150 feet.

Then he took me to the north side. There was another gate facing north, leaving the outer courtyard. He measured its length and width. It had three little rooms on each side. Its posts and porch were the same as the first gate: 87.5 feet by 43.75 feet. The windows and palm trees were identical to the east gate. It had seven steps leading up to it, and its porch faced inward. Across from this gate was a gate to the inner courtyard, on the north just like on the east. The distance between the two was 175 feet.

Then he took me to the south side, to the south gate. He measured its posts and its porch. It was the same size as the others. The porch with its windows was the same size as the ones I already saw. It also had seven steps going up to it. Its porch opened onto the outer courtyard, with palm trees carved on its posts on both sides. Across from it, the gate for the inner court faced south. He measured the distance across the courtyard from gate to gate: 175 feet.

He led me into the inner courtyard through the south gate. He measured it and found it was the same as the outer ones. Its rooms, walls, and entry hall were the same. The gate and porch, with windows all around, measured 87.5 by 43.75 feet. The entry hall of each of the gates leading to the inner courtyard was 43.75 by 8.75 feet. Each entry hall faced the outer courtyard. Palm trees were carved on its doorposts. Eight steps led up to it.

He then took me to the inner courtyard on the east and measured the gate. It was identical to the others—rooms, walls, and entry hall all the same. The gate and entry hall had windows all around. It measured 87.5 by 43.75 feet. Its porch faced the outer courtyard. There were palm trees on the doorposts on both sides. And it had eight steps.

He brought me to the north gate and measured it: same measurements. The rooms, walls, and entry hall with its windows: 87.5 by 43.75 feet. Its porch faced the outer courtyard. There were palm trees on its doorposts on both sides. And it had eight steps.

There was a room with a door at the entry hall of the gate where they cleaned the burnt offerings. Two tables were inside the entry hall, one on each side, where they slaughtered the animals for burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. Two tables were also placed against both outside walls of the entry hall—so, four tables inside and four tables outside, eight tables in total for slaughtering the sacrificial animals. The four tables for the burnt offerings were 31.5 inches square and 21 inches high. The tools for slaughtering the animals were kept there. Meat hooks, three inches long, were fastened to the walls. The tables were for the sacrificial animals.

Right where the inner gate opened onto the inner courtyard, there were two rooms, one at the north gate facing south and one at the south gate facing north. The man told me, “The room facing south is for the priests in charge of the Temple. And the room facing north is for the priests in charge of the altar. These priests are the sons of Zadok, the only sons of Levi allowed to get close to God to serve him.”
He measured the inner courtyard: a perfect 175-foot square. The altar was in front of the Temple.

He led me to the porch of the Temple and measured the gateposts of the porch: 8.75 feet high on both sides. The entrance to the gate was 21 feet wide and its walls were 4.5 feet thick. The entry hall itself was 35 feet wide and 21 feet deep. Ten steps led up to the porch. Columns stood on each side of the gateposts.

title: God's New Temple Tour (Insane Details!)
paragraphs: So this guy brought me into the actual Temple and started measuring the doorposts. They were a massive ten and a half feet thick on each side. The entrance was a wide seventeen and a half feet, and the side walls were a solid eight and three-quarters feet thick.
He also measured the main Temple Sanctuary, which was seventy feet by thirty-five feet.

Then he went even deeper inside and measured the doorposts at that entrance. They were three and a half feet thick. The entrance itself was ten and a half feet wide, and the walls around it were a crazy twelve and a quarter feet thick. He measured the inner sanctuary, a perfect thirty-five-foot square, at the very back of the main one. He told me, "This is the Holy of Holies."

He measured the Temple wall, and it was ten and a half feet thick. The side rooms wrapping around the Temple were seven feet wide. These rooms were stacked three stories high, with thirty rooms on each floor. There were support beams around the Temple wall for the side rooms, but they were freestanding, not actually connected to the main wall. The side rooms got wider as you went up from the first to the third floor. A staircase went from the bottom floor, through the middle, all the way to the top.

I noticed the Temple was built on a raised base that was ten and a half feet thick all around, which was the foundation for the side rooms. The outer walls of these side rooms were eight and three-quarters feet thick. There was an open area, a thirty-five-foot-wide strip, between the Temple's side rooms and the priests' rooms that went all the way around. The side rooms had two entrances from this open area, one on the north side and one on the south. There was an eight-and-three-quarters-foot open space all around.

The building that faced the Temple courtyard on the west was one hundred twenty-two and a half feet wide, with walls that were eight and three-quarters feet thick. The total length of the wall and building was one hundred fifty-seven and a half feet.

He measured the Temple, and it was one hundred seventy-five feet long. The Temple courtyard and the building, including its walls, also measured one hundred seventy-five feet. The width of the front of the Temple and the open area to the east was one hundred seventy-five feet.

He measured the length of the building at the back of the Temple, the one facing the courtyard, including its shelters on each side: one hundred seventy-five feet. The main Sanctuary, the inner Sanctuary, and the vestibule facing the courtyard were all paneled with wood. They had window frames and door frames in all three sections. The walls were paneled from the floor up to the windows. Above the entrance to the inner Sanctuary and on the walls all around both sanctuaries, there were carvings of angel-cherubim and palm trees at regular intervals, in an alternating pattern.

Each angel-cherub had two faces: a human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other. This design was carved all over the entire Temple. The cherubim and palm tree pattern was carved on the wall of the main Sanctuary from the floor all the way up to the height of the door.

The main Sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe. In front of the Holy Place, there was something that looked like a wooden altar. It was five and a quarter feet high and three and a half feet square. Its corners, base, and sides were all made of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands before God."

Both the main Sanctuary and the Holy Place had double doors. Each door was made of two hinged leaves, so one set could swing inward and the other outward. The doors of the main Sanctuary were carved with angel-cherubim and palm trees. There was a wooden canopy in front of the vestibule outside. On both sides of the porch, there were narrow windows with carved palm trees in between them.

title: honored Rooms & Secret Measurements
paragraphs: So this guy took me north to the outer courtyard and showed me these rooms facing the open area and the building on the north side. The north building was massive, like 175 feet long and 87.5 feet wide. Then, across this 35-foot gap from the inner courtyard, there were these rooms stacked three stories high. In front of the rooms, there was this long hallway, 17.5 feet wide and 175 feet long, with entrances from the north. The top-floor rooms were a bit smaller because their balconies were bigger than the ones on the lower floors. And the third-floor rooms didn't have pillars like the ones in the courtyard, so they were more compact. There was also this outer wall running alongside the rooms for 87.5 feet. The rooms facing the outer courtyard were 87.5 feet long, but the ones closer to the main holy area were a full 175 feet long. You got into the ground-floor rooms from the east, coming in from the outer courtyard.

On the south side, it was basically a mirror image. Same setup with rooms and a walkway, just like the ones on the north side—same size, same doors, everything. The main entrance was on the east, leading to the hallway, just like the other side.

Then he told me, "The north and south rooms next to the open area are the holy rooms. It's where the priests who serve God eat the holy offerings. They keep all the sacred stuff there—the grain, sin, and guilt offerings. These rooms are set apart, totally holy space. After the priests go into the Sanctuary, they can't just walk back out into the main courtyard and hang with everyone. They have to change out of their special ministering clothes and put on their regular outfits first."
After he finished measuring everything inside the Temple area, he took me out the east gate and started measuring the outside. With his measuring stick, he measured the east side: 875 feet.
Then the north side: 875 feet.
Then the south side: 875 feet.
Finally, he went to the west side and measured it: 875 feet.
He measured the wall on all four sides. Each wall was 875 feet long. These walls were there to separate the holy stuff from the everyday, ordinary stuff.

title: God's Glory is Back, and It's LIT!
