paragraphs: The man brought me to the east gate, and whoa! The epic glory of the God of Israel was pouring in from the east. It sounded like a massive waterfall, and the whole earth was literally glowing with His glory. It looked exactly like what I had seen when He came to destroy the city, and just like what I had seen by the Kebar River. I was so overwhelmed that I fell face down on the ground.
The amazing glory of God streamed into the Temple through the east gate. The Spirit lifted me to my feet and led me into the inner courtyard, and the Temple was filled with the radiant glory of God!

I heard someone speaking to me from inside the Temple while the man stood beside me. He said, “Son of man, this is the place for my throne, where I will plant my feet. This is where I will live with the Israelites forever. Neither the people of Israel nor their kings will ever again disrespect my holy name with their unfaithfulness and the worthless idols their kings set up at all the shrines. When they put their worship places right next to mine, with only a thin wall between us, they dishonored my holy name with their disgusting practices. Is it any surprise that I destroyed them in my anger? So let them get rid of their unfaithful ways and the disgusting idols their kings introduced, and I will come and live with them forever.

“Son of man, tell the people of Israel all about the Temple so they will be ashamed of their rebellious lives. Have them study the layout. That will really hit them hard. Show them the entire plan of the Temple—its entrances and exits, its dimensions, its rules, and its laws. Draw a picture of it so they can see the design and its purpose, and live according to its design and intent.
“This is the law of the Temple: As it extends from the top of the mountain, everything around it becomes holy ground. Yes, this is the law, the very meaning, of the Temple.
“These are the measurements of the altar, using the long (twenty-one-inch) ruler. The gutter at its base is twenty-one inches deep and twenty-one inches wide, with a four-inch lip around its edge.

“The height of the altar is three and a half feet from the base to the first ledge, which is twenty inches wide. From the first ledge to the second ledge, it is seven feet high and twenty-one inches wide. The altar hearth is another seven feet high. Four horns stick up from the hearth, each twenty-one inches high.

“The top of the altar, the hearth, is a square, twenty-one by twenty-one feet. The upper ledge is also a square, twenty-four and a half feet on each side, with a ten-and-a-half-inch lip and a twenty-one-inch-wide gutter all the way around.
“The steps of the altar go up from the east.”
Then the man said to me, “Son of man, God, the Master, says: ‘These are the rules for the altar when it is built, for sacrificing burnt offerings and sprinkling blood on it.

“‘For a sin offering, give a bull to the priests, the Levitical priests from the family of Zadok who come into my presence to serve me. Take some of its blood and smear it on the four horns of the altar that stick out from the four corners of the top ledge and all around the lip. This is to purify the altar and make it ready for the sacrifice. Then take the bull for the sin offerings and burn it in the designated place in the courtyard outside the Sanctuary.

“‘On the second day, offer a male goat without any defects for a sin offering. Purify the altar the same way you purified it for the bull. Then, when you have purified it, offer a bull without any defects and a ram without any defects from the flock. Present them before God. Sprinkle salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to God.

“‘For seven days, prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, and also a bull and a ram from the flock, animals without any defects. For seven days, the priests are to prepare the altar for its work, purifying it. This is how you dedicate it.

“‘After these seven days of dedication, from the eighth day on, the priests will present your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. And I will accept you with pleasure and delight! This is a decree from God, the Master.’”

title: honored Access Only: God's New Rules for the Temple
paragraphs: So then, the guy took me back to the outer gate of the Sanctuary, the one facing east. But it was shut tight.

God told me, "This gate is shut and it's staying shut. No one gets to go through it because I, the God of Israel, went through it. It stays shut. Only the prince, since he's the prince, can sit there and eat in God's presence. He has to enter the gate area through the porch and leave the same way."

Then the man led me through the north gate to the front of the Temple. I looked, and—whoa!—the radiant Glory of God was just filling the entire Temple of God! I immediately dropped to my face and worshiped.

God said to me, "Son of man, get a grip. Open your eyes, use your ears, and pay close attention to everything I'm about to tell you about the rules of this Temple of God, how all the laws work, the instructions for it, and all the entrances and exits of the Sanctuary.

"Go tell this crew of rebels, the house of Israel, 'A message from the Master God: That's enough of all your disgusting practices, Israel. You've been bringing foreigners who are uncommitted in their hearts and lives into my Sanctuary, desecrating it while you offer me my food—the fat and the blood. You've broken my covenant with all your vile acts. You haven't been taking care of my holy things. Instead, you put others in charge of my Sanctuary. So this is what the Master God says: No foreigner, uncommitted in heart and life, is to enter my Sanctuary, not even any foreigner living among the Israelites.'

"And as for the Levites who bailed on me when Israel went astray, who left me for their idols, they're going to have to face the consequences. They can still serve in my Sanctuary, guarding the temple gates and doing the work of the temple; they can slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before them to serve. But because they served them in front of their idols and caused the house of Israel to fall into sin, I've sworn an oath against them, declares the Master God, that they will bear their guilt. They are not to come near me to serve as priests or to touch any of my holy things or my most holy offerings; they will carry the shame of the disgusting things they've done. I'm putting them in charge of the maintenance of the temple, for all its work and everything that needs to be done in it.

"But the Levitical priests from the line of Zadok, who faithfully took care of my Sanctuary when the rest of Israel wandered off from me, they are the ones who will come into my presence to serve me. They will stand before me to offer the fat and the blood, declares the Master God. They are the only ones who can enter my Sanctuary; they alone will approach my table to serve me and carry out my duties.

"When they enter the gates of the inner courtyard, they have to wear linen clothes. They can't wear any wool while they're on duty in the inner courtyard gates or inside the temple. They'll wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments. They can't wear anything that makes them sweat. When they go out to the outer courtyard to the people, they have to take off the clothes they were serving in and leave them in the holy rooms. They need to change into regular clothes so they don't make the people holy just by touching them with their sacred garments.
"They can't shave their heads or let their hair get all long and messy; they have to keep their hair trimmed.
"No priest is allowed to drink wine when he enters the inner courtyard.
"They can't marry a widow or a divorced woman. They can only marry a virgin from the people of Israel, or the widow of a priest.
"Their job is to teach my people the difference between what's holy and what's not, and show them how to tell the difference between what's unclean and clean.
"In any dispute, the priests will act as judges and make decisions based on my rules. They will follow my laws and my decrees for all my appointed festivals, and they will keep my Sabbaths holy.

"A priest isn't supposed to make himself unclean by going near a dead body, unless it's his own father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister. For them, it's okay. After he's been purified, he has to wait seven days. Then, on the day he goes back into the Sanctuary, into the inner courtyard to serve, he has to offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Master God.

"As for their inheritance, I am their inheritance. You're not to give them any property in Israel; I am their possession. They will eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything in Israel that is devoted to God will be theirs. The very best of all the firstfruits and of every offering you bring will belong to the priests. You are to give the first of your ground meal to the priests so that a blessing may rest on your homes.
"The priests are not to eat any bird or animal that has died naturally or has been torn by wild animals."

title: The Ultimate Land Division & Offerings Guide
paragraphs: "When you guys are splitting up the land, you gotta set aside a massive chunk of it as sacred space for God: like, seven miles long and six miles wide. That whole area is holy ground. Inside this huge rectangle, block off a 750-foot square just for the Sanctuary, and give it a 750-foot buffer zone all around it. Then, mark off a section inside the sacred reserve that's seven miles long and three miles wide. That's where the Sanctuary and the Holy of Holies are gonna go. This is the spot where the priests will live—the guys who lead worship and serve God there. Their houses will be right there next to The Holy Place.

"Just north of that sacred reserve, block off an area about seven miles long and two and a quarter miles wide. That's for the Levites' villages, since they handle all the behind-the-scenes stuff for worship in the Sanctuary.
"Then, south of the sacred reserve, measure out a section seven miles long and about a mile and a half wide for the city itself. That area belongs to everyone in the whole family of Israel.

"Now for the prince: he gets the land right next to the east and west borders of that central sacred square. His land stretches all the way east to the Jordan River and all the way west to the Mediterranean Sea. That's his personal property in Israel. My princes are officially done bullying my people and walking all over them. They're gonna respect the land exactly how it was handed out to the tribes.

"This is the Message from God, the Master: 'I've had enough of your nonsense, princes of Israel! Stop bullying and taking advantage of my people. For once, just do what's fair and right. Use honest scales—no scamming with fake weights or rigged measurements. A pound needs to actually be sixteen ounces. A gallon needs to actually be four quarts. The ounce is the standard for both. And your money needs to be legit—no fake coins!

"‘Here's the deal on the offerings you guys need to bring: one-sixtieth of your wheat, one-sixtieth of your barley, one-hundredth of your oil, and one sheep out of every two hundred from Israel's best pastures. These are gonna be used for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make things right for the people. That's a direct order from God, the Master.

"‘Literally everyone in the land has to chip in for these special offerings, and the prince of Israel is in charge of managing them. It's the prince's job to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at all the big events—the Holy Festivals, the New Moons, and the Sabbaths. Basically, all the mandatory parties for the people of Israel. He's responsible for the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the people.

"‘This is the Message from God, the Master: On the first day of the first month, grab a flawless young bull and purify the Sanctuary. The priest is gonna take some blood from the sin offerings and rub it on the Temple doorposts, the four corners of the altar's ledge, and the gate entrance to the inner courtyard. Do this exact same ritual on the seventh day of the month for anyone who messes up by accident. That's how you make atonement for the Temple.
"‘On the fourteenth day of the first month, you're gonna celebrate the Passover. It's a massive seven-day feast. During the whole thing, you're only eating bread made without yeast.

"‘On Passover, the prince has to supply a bull as a sin offering for himself and everyone else in the country. Every single day of that seven-day feast, he's gotta provide seven flawless bulls and seven flawless rams as a burnt offering to God, plus one male goat every day.
"‘He also has to supply about five and a half gallons of grain offering and a gallon of oil for every single bull and ram.
"‘Then, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and for all seven days of that feast, he has to supply the exact same stuff for the sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.’"

title: honored Access Only: God's Temple Rules
paragraphs: Alright, here's a message from God, the Master: The east gate of the inner courtyard is locked on workdays, but it's open on the Sabbath and the New Moon. The prince will come in through the gate's entrance and stand by the gateposts while the priests present his offerings. He'll worship there on the porch and then head out, but the gate stays open until evening. On Sabbaths and New Moons, the people are to worship God at the entrance of that same gate.

The prince needs to provide the burnt offering for the Sabbath: six perfect lambs and a perfect ram. The grain offering with the ram is about five and a half gallons plus a gallon of oil, and a handful of grain for each lamb.

For the New Moon, he's to provide a young bull, six lambs, and a ram, all flawless. He'll also supply five and a half gallons of grain and a gallon of oil for both the ram and the bull, and a handful of grain for each lamb.
When the prince enters, he'll go through the entrance hall of the gate and leave the same way.

But when the people come to worship at the big feasts, anyone who enters through the north gate has to exit through the south gate, and anyone who enters through the south gate has to exit through the north. You can't leave the way you came in; you have to use the opposite gate. The prince will be right there with them, part of the crowd.
At the festivals and feasts, the grain offering is five and a half gallons with a gallon of oil for the bull and ram, and a handful of grain for each lamb.

When the prince wants to give a freewill offering to God, the east gate will be opened for him. He'll make his offering just like he does on the Sabbath. Then he'll leave, and they'll shut the gate after him.

Every morning, you're to bring a perfect one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering to God. Also, every morning, bring a grain offering of about a gallon of grain with a quart of oil to moisten it. This is a regular thing. The lamb, the grain, and the oil are a daily ritual.

Here's another message from God, the Master: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it stays in the family. But if he gives a gift to a servant, the servant only has it until the year of liberation, the Jubilee year. After that, it goes back to the prince. His inheritance is only for his sons. The prince can't just take land from the people. He can only give his sons what he already owns. None of my people should be forced off their land.

Then the man led me through the north gate to the holy rooms for the priests and showed me a room at the back to the west. He said, 'This is the kitchen where the priests will cook the guilt and sin offerings and bake the grain offering. This way, they don't have to do it in the main courtyard and accidentally endanger the people out there with holy stuff.'

He then took me to the outer courtyard and to each of its four corners. In each corner, there was another smaller court. These four smaller courts were all the same size, about sixty by forty-five feet. Around the inside walls of these courts was a stone shelf, and under the shelves were places to cook.
He told me, 'These are the kitchens where the Temple servants will cook the people's sacrifices.'

title: This River is GOATED
paragraphs: Alright, so this guy takes me back to the Temple entrance, and get this—I see water just pouring out from under the Temple porch, heading east (since the Temple faced east). The stream was coming from the south side of the Temple, just south of the altar. Then he takes me out through the north gate, leads me around the outside to the east gate complex, and whoa—the water was seriously gushing from the south side.

He walks east with a measuring tape and marks off about 1,500 feet. He leads me through the water, which is only ankle-deep. He measures another 1,500 feet, and now the water's up to my knees. Another 1,500 feet, and it's up to my waist. He measures another 1,500 feet, and by this point, it's a whole river. It's way over my head, deep enough to swim in—like, no way you could walk through it.
He asks me, "Son of man, you getting a good look at this?"
Then he brings me back to the riverbank. As I'm sitting there, I notice tons of trees on both sides of the river.

He tells me, "This water flows east, down to the Arabah valley, and then into the Dead Sea. When it hits that stagnant water, the sea will become fresh. Everywhere this river goes, life will just explode—huge schools of fish—because it's turning the salty sea into fresh water. Life just thrives wherever the river flows. Fishermen will be lined up shoulder to shoulder along the shore, from En Gedi all the way to En-eglaim, casting their nets. The sea will be packed with all kinds of fish, just like the Mediterranean.
"But the swamps and marshes won't get fresh. They're gonna stay salty.

"But along the river itself, on both banks, all kinds of fruit trees will grow. Their leaves will never wilt, and they'll never stop producing fruit. They'll have a new crop every single month because the river from the Sanctuary feeds them. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves will be for healing."

This is a message from the Lord, the Master: "These are the borders you'll use to divide the land for the twelve tribes of Israel, and Joseph gets two shares. You'll divide it up equally. I made a solemn promise to give it to your ancestors, and I swore this land would be your inheritance.
"Here are the land boundaries:

"The northern border runs from the Mediterranean Sea along the Hethlon road to the turnoff for Hamath's entrance, then to Zedad, Berothah, and Sibraim (which is between Damascus and Hamath territories), and then on to Hazor-hatticon on the Hauran border. The boundary goes from the Sea to Hazor-enon, with Damascus and Hamath to the north. That's the northern border.
"The eastern border runs between Damascus and Hauran, down the Jordan River between Gilead and the land of Israel, all the way to the Dead Sea, as far as Tamar. That's the eastern border.
"The southern border runs west from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, follows the Brook of Egypt, and goes out to the Mediterranean Sea. That's the southern border.
"The western border is just the Mediterranean Sea, from the southern border north to the point where the road turns east towards the entrance of Hamath. That's the western border.

"You're to divide this land among the twelve tribes of Israel. Split it up as your inheritance, and you have to include the foreigners who have settled among you and had kids. Treat them just like they were born there. They get an inheritance among the tribes of Israel too. Whatever tribe the foreigner lives in, that's where they get their inheritance. This is a decree from the Lord, the Master."

title: The Ultimate Land Distribution
paragraphs: Alright, here's the breakdown for the tribes:

First up, Dan gets a slice of land. It's up on the northern border, following the Hethlon road that cuts over to the entrance of Hamath, going all the way to Hazor-enon. This means the territory of Damascus is to the north, next to Hamath, with the northern border stretching from the east to the west.
Asher gets a piece of the action too, bordering Dan's territory from east to west.
Naphtali is next, with a portion of land that borders Asher from east to west.
Then there's Manasseh, whose land borders Naphtali from east to west.
Ephraim gets a portion that borders Manasseh from east to west.
Reuben's portion borders Ephraim from east to west.
And Judah's portion borders Reuben from east to west.

Now, right next to Judah's territory, from east to west, is this special sacred area that you're gonna set aside. It's a square, about seven by seven miles, and the Sanctuary is gonna be right in the middle. This holy area for God will be seven miles long and just under three miles wide.

Here's how it's getting divided up. The priests get the area that's seven miles on the north and south sides, and a bit over three miles wide on the east and west sides. God's Sanctuary will be at the center of it. This is for the priests who are set apart, the descendants of Zadok who stayed loyal and served me, and didn't wander off like the other Levites did when Israel went off the rails. This is their special piece of the land, a gift from the land itself, super holy ground, right next to the Levites' section.

The Levites get a section that's the same size as the priests' land, roughly seven by three miles. But here's the rule: they can't sell or trade any of it. It's the best part of the land, not to mention it's holy to God.

Whatever is left of that 'sacred square'—each side is seven miles by a mile and a half—is for regular use. That's for the city and its buildings, with some open country around it, but the city itself is in the center. The north, south, east, and west sides of the city are each about a mile and a half long. There will be a strip of pasture, 125 yards wide, surrounding the city on all sides. The rest of this area, three miles of countryside to the east and west of the sacred zone, is for farming. It'll provide food for the city. People from all the tribes of Israel will come and work the fields.
This whole dedicated area, set apart for holy purposes, will be a square, seven miles by seven miles, a 'holy square,' and it includes the part for the city.

The rest of the land, the country stretching east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea from the seven-mile sides of the 'holy square,' belongs to the prince. His land is squeezed between the tribal lands to the north and south, and it extends both east and west from the 'sacred square' with the Temple in the middle. The land for the Levites on one side and the city on the other is in the middle of the prince's territory. The 'sacred square' is flanked on the east and west by the prince's land and bordered on the north and south by the territories of Judah and Benjamin.
And now for the rest of the tribes:
Benjamin gets one portion, stretching from the eastern to the western boundary.
Simeon gets a portion, bordering Benjamin from east to west.
Issachar gets a portion, bordering Simeon from east to west.
Zebulun gets a portion, bordering Issachar from east to west.
Gad gets a portion, bordering Zebulun from east to west.
The southern border of Gad will run south from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, follow the Brook of Egypt, and then go out to the great Mediterranean Sea.
This is the land you're supposed to divide up among the tribes of Israel for them to inherit. These are their portions. That's a decree from God, the Master.

And these are the gates of the city. On the north side, which is 2,250 yards long (and the city gates are named after the tribes of Israel), there are three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, which is also 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, measuring 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, also 2,250 yards, there are three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The four sides of the city add up to a total of nearly six miles.
And from now on, the name of the city will be Yahweh-Shammah:
God-Is-There.
